quote: Foreign sponsors must designate a US Agent per 21 CFR 600.4.
error: 21 CFR 600.4 does not exist. Part 600 Subpart A has only 600.2 and 600.3.
correct: The US agent requirement for foreign establishments is in establishment registration regulations, e.g. 21 CFR 207.69 (drugs, including biologics) and 21 CFR 607.40 (blood). It is not in 21 CFR 600.

quote: Per 21 CFR 600.4, each foreign establishment must designate a United States agent who resides or maintains a place of business in the US.
error: 21 CFR 600.4 does not exist.
correct: Cite 21 CFR 207.69(b) (or 607.40 for blood establishments) for the foreign-establishment US agent requirement.

quote: Typically a minimum of 3 consecutive commercial-scale batches are required for process validation.
error: FDA's 2011 Process Validation guidance dropped the fixed three-batch expectation. No minimum batch number is required, and the number of PPQ batches must be justified scientifically and by risk.
correct: The number of PPQ batches is not fixed by FDA and must be justified using process knowledge and risk (2011 Process Validation guidance). Three is common in practice but is not required.

quote: Testing must include potency, sterility, endotoxin, identity, and general safety (where required). Some tests may be waived under specific circumstances per 21 CFR 610.1(b).
error: General safety testing (610.11) no longer exists. 21 CFR 610.1 is a single paragraph with no paragraph (b), and it does not provide test waivers.
correct: Testing covers potency (610.10), sterility (610.12), purity/pyrogens (610.13) and identity (610.14). Alternatives to prescribed tests go through 21 CFR 610.9 (equivalent methods) or 640.120 (exceptions).

quote:
{ value: 'required', label: 'Required (per 21 CFR 610.11)' },
              { value: 'waived', label: 'Waived (per 21 CFR 610.11(g))' },
error: The general safety test requirement in 21 CFR 610.11 (and the 610.11(g) exemption) was removed by FDA final rule in 2015 (80 FR 37971, July 2, 2015). 610.11 is now reserved. A general safety test is neither 'required per 610.11' nor 'waived per 610.11(g)'.
correct: FDA removed the general safety test (610.11) in 2015, so no GST is required under 21 CFR 610. Any test for abnormal toxicity is now product-specific, set in the license or a monograph.

quote: The general safety test (formerly abnormal toxicity test) may be waived if alternative methods provide equivalent assurance of safety.
error: The text says the GST is still in force and only waivable. It was removed from the regulations entirely in 2015.
correct: The 21 CFR 610.11 general safety test requirement was removed in 2015. Nothing remains to waive.

quote: Reproductive toxicology requirements follow ICH S6(R1) Section 4.4
error: In ICH S6(R1) Part I, Section 4.4 is Repeated Dose Toxicity Studies. Reproductive performance and developmental toxicity is Section 4.6, and Part II (Addendum) covers it in Section 5.
correct: Cite ICH S6(R1) Part I Section 4.6 and Part II (Addendum) Section 5 for reproductive and developmental toxicity.

quote: reference: 'FDA Guidance on Immunogenicity Assessment (2019)',
error: The 2019 FDA guidance is on immunogenicity testing (ADA assay development and validation). The Immunogenicity Assessment for Therapeutic Protein Products guidance dates from 2014.
correct: FDA Guidance: Immunogenicity Testing of Therapeutic Protein Products — Developing and Validating Assays for Anti-Drug Antibody Detection (2019).

quote: Per 21 CFR 601.14 (Required Postmarketing Reports), 21 CFR 601.70 (Annual Reports for Biological Products),
error: 21 CFR 601.14 is 'Regulatory submissions in electronic format', not required postmarketing reports. 21 CFR 601.70 is 'Annual progress reports of postmarketing studies', not general annual reports for biological products.
correct: Postmarketing safety reporting for biologics is 21 CFR 600.80. 601.70 covers annual progress reports on postmarketing studies. PMR authority comes from FDCA 505(o)(3), PREA, 21 CFR 601.41 and 601.91.

quote: The Accelerated Approval Integrity Act (2023) strengthens FDA authority to require and enforce timely completion of confirmatory studies. Periodic safety update reports (PSUR/PADER) are required per ICH E2C(R2).
error: The accelerated approval reforms became law as part of the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2022 (FDORA, inside the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023, signed 2022-12-29). The 'Accelerated Approval Integrity Act' was a bill that was not enacted under that name. In the US, periodic safety reports for biologics are required by 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2) (PAER), not by ICH E2C(R2). E2C(R2) replaced the PSUR with the PBRER.
correct: FDORA (2022) section 3210 amended FDCA 506(c) to strengthen confirmatory-study requirements. Periodic adverse experience reports are required under 21 CFR 600.80(c)(2), and an ICH E2C(R2) PBRER may be submitted in their place under an FDA waiver.

quote: List FDA-required post-marketing studies or clinical trials under 21 CFR 601.14.
error: 21 CFR 601.14 covers electronic-format submissions. It does not authorize postmarketing requirements.
correct: PMRs arise under FDCA 505(o)(3), PREA (21 USC 355c), 21 CFR 601.41 (accelerated approval) and 601.91 (Animal Rule).

quote: Under the Accelerated Approval Integrity Act (2023), FDA has enhanced authority to withdraw approval
error: No statute named the Accelerated Approval Integrity Act was enacted. The authority came from FDORA 2022.
correct: Under FDORA (2022), which amended FDCA 506(c), FDA has expedited withdrawal authority when confirmatory studies are not conducted with due diligence.

quote: Form FDA 356h (Application to Market a New Drug, Biologic, or Antibiotic Drug for Human Use)
error: This is the obsolete title of Form 356h. Antibiotic applications were folded into NDAs by FDAMA 1997.
correct: Form FDA 356h: Application to Market a New or Abbreviated New Drug or Biologic for Human Use.

quote: The FDA statistical tiered approach includes: Tier 1 (equivalence testing for most critical attributes like potency and protein content), Tier 2 (quality range approach), and Tier 3 (raw data comparison).
error: The tiered statistical approach is not in the 2015 Scientific Considerations guidance. It came from the 2017 draft guidance 'Statistical Approaches to Evaluate Analytical Similarity', which FDA withdrew in June 2018 and replaced with the comparative analytical assessment draft guidance (2019, revised 2024), which does not use the tier framework.
correct: Current FDA recommendations (Comparative Analytical Assessment and Other Quality-Related Considerations draft guidance) use a risk-based approach with equivalence testing or quality-range methods per attribute, not the withdrawn Tier 1/2/3 scheme.

quote: Per FDA Guidance: Clinical Pharmacology Data to Support a Demonstration of Biosimilarity to a Reference Product (2014) and 42 USC 262(k), the clinical development program for a biosimilar typically includes a comparative PK similarity study (first clinical study), followed by at least one comparative clinical study in a sensitive patient population.
error: The clinical pharmacology guidance was finalized in December 2016 (2014 was the draft). FDA's October 2025 draft guidance on assessing the need for comparative efficacy studies says such studies are generally not needed when analytical and PK similarity are shown, so 'at least one comparative clinical study' is no longer the typical expectation.
correct: Cite the December 2016 final guidance. Under current FDA thinking (2025 draft), a comparative efficacy study is generally not expected when comparative analytical assessment and PK/immunogenicity data establish biosimilarity.

quote: Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA, 5 USC Appendix 2)
error: FACA was recodified in December 2022 (Pub. L. 117-286) from 5 U.S.C. App. 2 to 5 U.S.C. chapter 10. 'Appendix 2' is the superseded citation.
correct: Federal Advisory Committee Act, 5 U.S.C. §§ 1001–1014 (formerly 5 U.S.C. App. 2).

quote: { value: 'pcns', label: 'PCNS — Psychopharmacologic Drugs AC' }
error: PCNS is the acronym for the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee. The Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee is a separate committee, abbreviated PDAC.
correct: PCNS = Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee; PDAC = Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee (they are separate options).

quote: { value: 'dermatologic', label: 'DDMAC — Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs AC' }
error: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee is abbreviated DODAC. DDMAC was the acronym of CDER's former Division of Drug Marketing, Advertising, and Communications, which is not an advisory committee.
correct: DODAC — Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee.

quote: For NDA/BLA submissions, FDA expects at least 1,500 patients exposed and 300-600 patients for 6 months per ICH E1.
error: ICH E1 does not apply to all NDA/BLA submissions. Its exposure numbers (about 1,500 total, 300-600 for 6 months, 100 for 1 year) cover only drugs intended for long-term (chronic or repeated intermittent) treatment of non-life-threatening conditions. Applying them to every NDA/BLA, including oncology, is wrong.
correct: ICH E1's exposure expectations (about 1,500 total; 300-600 for 6 months; at least 100 for 1 year) apply to drugs intended for long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions; they are not a general NDA/BLA requirement.

quote: Present an integrated safety summary across all studies per ICH E2C(R2).
error: ICH E2C(R2) is the guideline for the Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report (PBRER), a post-marketing periodic report. It does not govern the pre-approval integrated summary of safety.
correct: The integrated safety summary is governed by ICH M4E(R2) (CTD Module 2.7.4 Summary of Clinical Safety) and, for an NDA, by 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a) (Integrated Summary of Safety).

quote: The framework evaluates five dimensions: (1) Analysis of Condition, (2) Current Treatment Options, (3) Benefit, (4) Risk, and (5) Risk Management.
error: FDA's Benefit-Risk Framework as implemented under PDUFA VI (2018 plan) and the 2023 draft guidance has four dimensions; Risk and Risk Management are one dimension. The five-dimension version is the older PDUFA V (2013) layout. The 2023 draft guidance is titled 'Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products'. 'Benefit-Risk Assessment in Drug Regulatory Decision-Making' is the title of the 2018 PDUFA VI implementation plan, not a 2023 draft revision.
correct: Four dimensions: Analysis of Condition, Current Treatment Options, Benefit, and Risk and Risk Management, followed by conclusions (2018 PDUFA VI implementation plan; 2023 draft guidance 'Benefit-Risk Assessment for New Drug and Biological Products').

quote: FDA's Benefit-Risk Framework (PDUFA VI) recommends a structured summary table with five dimensions: Analysis of Condition, Current Treatment Options, Benefit, Risk, and Risk Management.
error: The PDUFA VI Benefit-Risk Framework has four dimensions; Risk and Risk Management form one combined dimension.
correct: Four dimensions: Analysis of Condition, Current Treatment Options, Benefit, Risk and Risk Management.

quote: Per FDA guidance, presenters should include the lead clinician, lead statistician, and lead safety scientist.
error: No FDA guidance specifies which roles the sponsor's presenters must hold. Who presents is the sponsor's choice, and this is industry practice presented as FDA guidance.
correct: Industry practice is often to field clinical, statistical and safety leads; FDA guidance does not prescribe the sponsor's presenters.

quote: at least 12 months of long-term stability data and 6 months of accelerated data are required at the time of NDA/BLA submission
error: The 12-month minimum comes from ICH Q1A(R2) and applies to NDAs. Biotechnology products in a BLA fall under ICH Q5C, which requires at least 6 months of real-time data on the proposed storage condition at submission (for a proposed storage period of more than 6 months).
correct: For NDAs (ICH Q1A(R2)): at least 12 months long-term and 6 months accelerated data at submission. For biotech BLAs (ICH Q5C): at least 6 months of real-time data at submission, with data continuing through the proposed shelf life.

quote: Per ICH Q3C(R8), classify all solvents
error: ICH Q3C(R8) has been superseded. Q3C(R9) reached Step 4 in January 2024.
correct: ICH Q3C(R9)

quote: ICH Q3A(R2) Impurities in New Drug Substances, Section 5
error: Q3A(R2) Section 5 is 'Reporting Impurity Content of Batches'. Qualification of impurities is Section 7.
correct: ICH Q3A(R2) Section 7 (Qualification of Impurities), together with Attachments 1 and 3

quote: control strategy (Option 1–5 per ICH M7)
error: ICH M7(R2) Section 8.1 defines four control options, not five. The option labels at lines 782-786 are also wrong: 'Option 1 — Avoid', 'Option 3 — Control in drug substance spec' and 'Option 5 — Wider limit (LTL, clinical trial)' do not match the guideline, and there is no Option 5. Line 789 cites 'ICH M7(R2) Table 1' for the control options, but Table 1 is the impurity classification (Classes 1-5).
correct: ICH M7(R2) Section 8.1 control options: Option 1 = test in the drug substance specification. Option 2 = test in a starting material, intermediate or in-process specification at or below the acceptable limit. Option 3 = test upstream with a higher limit, supported by purge understanding. Option 4 = control through process understanding and purge, with no testing. Less-than-lifetime limits come from Section 7.3 and Table 2, not from a control option.

quote: Per FDA Process Validation Guidance (2011, updated 2021)
error: There was no 2021 update. The current version is the January 2011 guidance (Revision 1). The same wrong 'Rev. 2021' citation appears at lines 1183 and 1192.
correct: FDA Guidance for Industry: Process Validation: General Principles and Practices (January 2011, Rev. 1)

quote: Per FDA guidance, a minimum of 3 consecutive PPQ batches at commercial scale is typically expected
error: FDA's 2011 Process Validation guidance deliberately sets no minimum number of PPQ batches. It dropped the old 'three consecutive batches' convention and asks the manufacturer to justify the number from process knowledge and risk.
correct: FDA's Process Validation guidance (2011) sets no minimum number of PPQ batches. The number must be justified by process understanding and variability. Three batches is common industry practice, not an FDA requirement.

quote: The EudraCT number is required for studies conducted in the EU per Regulation (EU) No 536/2014.
error: The EudraCT number belongs to the Clinical Trials Directive 2001/20/EC. Under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, trials are identified by an EU CT number assigned in CTIS.
correct: Under Regulation (EU) 536/2014 the EU CT number (CTIS) is required; EudraCT numbers apply to legacy Directive 2001/20/EC trials.

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 9.4.3, the comparator should be described in sufficient detail
error: ICH E3 9.4.3 is Method of Assigning Patients to Treatment Groups. Comparator identity is in 9.4.2.
correct: ICH E3 Section 9.4.2 (Identity of Investigational Product(s)), including comparator and placebo.

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 10.1, the CSR must list all protocol amendments, classifying each as major or minor
error: ICH E3 10.1 is Disposition of Patients. Protocol amendments go in 9.8 (Changes in the Conduct of the Study or Planned Analyses), with the amendments themselves in Appendix 16.1.1. E3 does not require a major/minor classification. The same wrong 10.1 citation appears at line 436.
correct: ICH E3 Section 9.8 (Changes in the Conduct of the Study or Planned Analyses) and Appendix 16.1.1.

quote: FDA Guidance "Major/Minor Amendments to IND" (2001)
error: No FDA guidance with this title exists. Requirements for IND protocol amendments are in 21 CFR 312.30.
correct: 21 CFR 312.30 (Protocol amendments); no 'Major/Minor Amendments to IND' guidance exists.

quote: FDA Guidance "Oversight of Clinical Investigations" (2013) emphasizes the importance of documenting the screen failure rate to assess the generalizability of the trial population.
error: The 2013 FDA guidance 'Oversight of Clinical Investigations — A Risk-Based Approach to Monitoring' is about sponsor monitoring. It does not address screen failure rates as a measure of generalizability.
correct: Generalizability and eligibility criteria are addressed in FDA 'Enhancing the Diversity of Clinical Trial Populations' (2020) and ICH E3 10.1 / CONSORT, not the 2013 risk-based monitoring guidance.

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 11.3, the CSR must document prior therapies and concomitant medications ... Per ICH E3 Section 11.3.2, prohibited medications
error: ICH E3 11.3 is Measurements of Treatment Compliance, and there is no 11.3.2. Prior and concomitant therapy is in 9.4.7 (protocol plan) and 11.2 (with demographic and baseline characteristics). Line 771 repeats the wrong 11.3 citation.
correct: ICH E3 Section 9.4.7 (Prior and Concomitant Therapy) and Section 11.2; 11.3 = Measurements of Treatment Compliance.

quote: Per ICH E9(R1) and FDA Guidance "Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials" (2020), missing data > 20% may compromise the validity of the primary analysis.
error: No 2020 FDA guidance has this title. FDA's 'Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials' is its 1998 adoption of ICH E9, and E9(R1) was finalized by FDA in 2021. Neither sets a 20% missing-data threshold. The same non-existent 2020 guidance is cited at line 1695.
correct: ICH E9 (FDA guidance 1998) / E9(R1) addendum (FDA final 2021); neither sets a numeric missing-data threshold.

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Preventing Missing Data in Clinical Trials" (2010)
error: No FDA guidance has this title. The 2010 document is the National Research Council report 'The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials', which FDA commissioned.
correct: National Research Council (2010), 'The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials'; ICH E9(R1).

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 12.1, present AE data by System Organ Class (SOC) and Preferred Term (PT) using MedDRA coding.
error: ICH E3 12.1 is Extent of Exposure. AE displays and analyses are in 12.2 (12.2.2 Display of Adverse Events, 12.2.3 Analysis of Adverse Events). The same wrong 12.1 citation for AE analysis appears again at lines 1210, 1227-1228 and 1240-1241.
correct: ICH E3 Section 12.2 (12.2.2 display / 12.2.3 analysis of adverse events); 12.1 = Extent of Exposure.

quote: Drug-related deaths require immediate regulatory notification per 21 CFR 312.32 (IND Safety Reports) within 7 calendar days of sponsor awareness. Ensure these have been reported to all regulatory authorities and IRBs/ECs.
error: Under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(2), the 7-calendar-day report applies only to UNEXPECTED fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reactions. An expected death (consistent with the IB) does not trigger it. 312.32 also requires notifying FDA and all participating investigators, not IRBs directly.
correct: Unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reactions: FDA notified within 7 calendar days, with the full IND safety report (FDA and all participating investigators) within 15 calendar days. Expected events are not 7-day reports.

quote: Hy's Law cases predict a drug-induced liver injury (DILI) rate of approximately 1 in 10,000 treated patients
error: The FDA DILI guidance (2009) gives no fixed rate of 1 in 10,000. It says the rate of severe DILI (death or transplant) is roughly one-tenth the Hy's Law case rate, so the implied incidence depends on database size. One case is worrisome and two are highly predictive.
correct: Per FDA DILI guidance (2009): roughly 10% of Hy's Law cases progress to death or transplant; one case is worrisome, two are considered highly predictive of severe DILI potential.

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 12.2.2, AESIs are pre-defined events warranting focused monitoring
error: ICH E3 12.2.2 is Display of Adverse Events and does not define AESIs. E3 uses 'other significant adverse events', in 12.3.
correct: ICH E3 12.2.2 = Display of Adverse Events; 'other significant AEs' are handled in 12.3. AESI is a CIOMS VI / protocol concept, not an E3 definition.

quote: Per ICH E1 Section 2.4, exposure-response analysis may be informative.
error: ICH E1 covers the extent of population exposure needed to assess safety for long-term treatment of non-life-threatening conditions. It does not cover exposure-response analysis. That is ICH E4 and the FDA exposure-response guidance.
correct: ICH E4 (Dose-Response Information to Support Drug Registration) / FDA Exposure-Response Relationships guidance (2003).

quote: individual patient narratives are required for: (1) ALL deaths, regardless of causality; (2) ALL SAEs assessed as drug-related by the investigator; (3) ALL AEs leading to discontinuation of study drug
error: ICH E3 12.3.2 asks for narratives of every death and every other serious adverse event, whatever the causality. It does not limit SAE narratives to drug-related ones. For other significant AEs, including those leading to discontinuation, it asks only for the ones judged of special interest because of clinical importance.
correct: ICH E3 12.3.2: brief narratives of each death, each other serious adverse event (regardless of causality), and those other significant adverse events judged to be of special interest because of clinical importance.

quote: All interim results must be reported in the CSR per ICH E3 Section 11.4.6.
error: ICH E3 11.4.6 is By-Patient Displays. Interim analyses and data monitoring are 11.4.2.3.
correct: ICH E3 Section 11.4.2.3 (Interim Analyses and Data Monitoring).

quote: EMA "Benefit-Risk Methodology" (GVP Module V)
error: GVP Module V is Risk Management Systems. EMA's Benefit-Risk Methodology Project is a separate EMA initiative, not a GVP module.
correct: GVP Module V = Risk management systems; EMA Benefit-Risk Methodology Project is separate (benefit-risk evaluation in PSURs is GVP Module VII).

quote: The FDA framework considers five dimensions: (1) Analysis of Condition, (2) Current Treatment Options, (3) Benefit, (4) Risk, and (5) Risk Management.
error: FDA's current Benefit-Risk Framework, used in the 2023 guidance, has four dimensions, with 'Risk and Risk Management' as one combined row. Splitting it in two is the earlier PDUFA V-era version.
correct: Four dimensions: Analysis of Condition, Current Treatment Options, Benefit, and Risk and Risk Management.

quote: Per FDASIA 2012, document any expedited designations granted for this product/indication.
error: FDASIA 2012 created Breakthrough Therapy only. Fast Track dates from FDAMA 1997, RMAT from the 21st Century Cures Act 2016, and Orphan designation from the Orphan Drug Act 1983. Orphan designation is not an expedited pathway.
correct: Breakthrough: FDASIA 2012; Fast Track: FDAMA 1997 (amended by FDASIA); RMAT: 21st Century Cures Act 2016; Orphan: Orphan Drug Act 1983; Accelerated approval: 21 CFR 314 Subpart H / 601 Subpart E.

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 13.1, the CSR conclusion should address
error: ICH E3 Section 13 (Discussion and Overall Conclusions) has no subsection 13.1.
correct: ICH E3 Section 13 (Discussion and Overall Conclusions), which has no numbered subsections.

quote: helpText: 'DEHP and phthalates require labeling per 21 CFR 801.437',
error: 21 CFR 801.437 is the labeling requirement for devices made with natural rubber latex. No CFR section requires DEHP or phthalate labeling.
correct: DEHP disclosure is a recommendation in FDA guidance (2002 safety assessment and DEHP-in-PVC device recommendations), not a 21 CFR 801 requirement. 801.437 applies to natural rubber latex.

quote: FDA\'s 2020 guidance on ISO 10993-1 emphasizes a risk-based approach
error: The 2020 version of FDA's guidance on Use of ISO 10993-1 was superseded by the September 2023 revision. Line 815 repeats the 2020 citation.
correct: FDA guidance 'Use of International Standard ISO 10993-1, Biological evaluation of medical devices - Part 1' (September 2023).

quote: { value: 'irritation', label: 'Irritation (ISO 10993-10)' },
error: Irritation testing was moved out of ISO 10993-10 into ISO 10993-23:2021. ISO 10993-10:2021 covers skin sensitization only.
correct: Irritation (ISO 10993-23)

quote: FDA may request evidence of design controls per 21 CFR 820.30 and quality system compliance
error: 21 CFR 820.30 was removed when the QMSR took effect on 2026-02-02. The text still cites it as in force.
correct: Under the QMSR (21 CFR 820 as amended, effective 2026-02-02), design and development requirements come from ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3, incorporated by reference through 21 CFR 820.10. 820.30 should be marked as former.

quote: label: 'Design Controls per 21 CFR 820.30 Documented',
error: The label cites the removed QSR section 820.30 as current.
correct: Design and development controls per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3, as incorporated by the QMSR (21 CFR 820.10). Former 21 CFR 820.30.

quote: helpText: 'Per 21 CFR 820.50 — purchasing controls for critical suppliers',
error: 21 CFR 820.50 (purchasing controls) was removed by the QMSR effective 2026-02-02.
correct: Purchasing controls per ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.4, as incorporated by the QMSR (21 CFR 820.10). Former 21 CFR 820.50.

quote: FDA\'s 2023 guidance on Content of Premarket Submissions for Device Software Functions updates the documentation requirements based on IEC 62304 software safety classification. ... The software safety classification (Class A, B, or C) determines the required level of documentation.
error: In the 2023 FDA software premarket guidance, the amount of documentation is set by the FDA Documentation Level (Basic or Enhanced), which comes from the device's risk. It is not set by the IEC 62304 safety class (A/B/C).
correct: The 2023 guidance replaced Level of Concern with a Documentation Level, Basic or Enhanced. Enhanced applies where a software failure could present a hazardous situation with probable risk of death or serious injury. IEC 62304 classes drive the 62304 process rigor, not the FDA submission documentation level.

quote: FDA\'s 2023 guidance "Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions" requires comprehensive cybersecurity documentation including a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
error: The September 2023 cybersecurity guidance was superseded by the final guidance of the same title issued in June 2025. The SBOM obligation also comes from statute (FD&C Act section 524B, for cyber devices), not from the guidance. Lines 1218, 1276, 1285 and 1286 repeat the 2023 citation.
correct: FDA, Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions (June 2025), which implements FD&C Act section 524B. The SBOM is a statutory requirement for cyber devices under 524B(b)(3).

quote: helpText: '5-day reports, 30-day reports, and annual certification',
error: 21 CFR 803 has no annual certification requirement. The annual certification provision was stayed and later revoked, and the current reports under Part 803 are 30-day, 5-day and supplemental reports.
correct: 5-day reports, 30-day reports, and supplemental/follow-up reports (21 CFR 803.50, 803.53, 803.56).

quote: helpText: 'Required for implantable devices to provide to patients',
error: US law has no general requirement for a patient implant card on implantable devices. The implant card obligation comes from EU MDR Article 18. A 510(k) flow presents it as an FDA requirement.
correct: A patient implant card is required under EU MDR 2017/745 Article 18. In the US it is required only where a device-specific special control or order calls for it, for example some patient labeling for MR Conditional implants.

quote: { value: 'class_ii_pma', label: 'Class II (transitional — PMA required)', description: 'Reclassified device requiring PMA' },
error: No Class II device category requires a PMA. Transitional devices (formerly regulated as drugs) were placed in Class III by FD&C Act 520(l). Reclassifying a device to Class II removes the PMA requirement, and those devices go through 510(k) or De Novo.
correct: PMA applies to Class III devices, including transitional devices deemed Class III under section 520(l). A device reclassified to Class II no longer requires a PMA.

quote: FDA may convene an advisory panel for novel or high-risk Class III devices per 21 CFR 814.44(e)
error: 21 CFR 814.44(e) covers the approvable letter. Panel referral is in 814.44(a), and the panel report in 814.44(b).
correct: 21 CFR 814.44(a): FDA may refer the PMA to an advisory panel, and will do so on the applicant's request unless the application substantially duplicates information a panel has already reviewed.

quote: Design controls per 21 CFR 820.30 are mandatory for Class III devices and are a critical component of the PMA review.
error: 21 CFR 820.30 (and its paragraphs (d), (f), (g), (h), (i), (j) cited at lines 445, 461, 468, 475, 482, 489, 496, 506-507, 515-516) was removed when the QMSR took effect on 2026-02-02. Part 820 now incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference (21 CFR 820.10). The citations are presented as in force, and the DHF requirement at '820.30(j)' no longer exists as a separate requirement.
correct: Design and development controls now come from ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3, incorporated by reference through 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR, effective 2026-02-02). Cite 820.30 only as the former QSR section.

quote: Manufacturing must comply with the Quality System Regulation (QSR) per 21 CFR 820. Special processes such as sterilization, welding, molding, and coating that cannot be fully verified by subsequent inspection and test must be validated per 21 CFR 820.75.
error: The QSR was replaced by the QMSR on 2026-02-02, and 21 CFR 820.75 no longer exists. The same removed section is cited as current at lines 565, 603-604 and 612-613.
correct: Part 820 is now the Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR), and process validation comes from ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.5.6, incorporated by reference through 21 CFR 820.10.

quote: Contract manufacturers must be qualified and subject to supplier controls per 21 CFR 820.50
error: 21 CFR 820.50 (purchasing controls) was removed by the QMSR effective 2026-02-02. It is also cited as current at line 661.
correct: Supplier and purchasing controls now come from ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.4, incorporated through 21 CFR 820.10.

quote: The PMA applicant must demonstrate compliance with the Quality System Regulation (21 CFR 820) and ideally ISO 13485:2016. ... Having an ISO 13485 certification from a recognized body provides additional confidence but does not replace 21 CFR 820 compliance.
error: Since 2026-02-02 Part 820 is the QMSR, which incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference. ISO 13485 is no longer 'ideally' an add-on to a separate QSR. The 'QSR' wording at lines 629, 632, 691-694 is also outdated.
correct: PMA applicants must comply with the QMSR (21 CFR 820, which incorporates ISO 13485:2016 plus FDA-specific requirements). Certification does not substitute for FDA inspection.

quote: CAPA System Established (21 CFR 820.90)
error: 21 CFR 820.90 was never the CAPA section (it covered nonconforming product; CAPA was 820.100), and both sections were removed by the QMSR on 2026-02-02.
correct: CAPA comes from ISO 13485:2016 clauses 8.5.2/8.5.3 through 21 CFR 820.10. It was formerly 21 CFR 820.100.

quote: Document Control System in Place (21 CFR 820.40)
error: 21 CFR 820.40 was removed by the QMSR effective 2026-02-02.
correct: Document control comes from ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4 through 21 CFR 820.10.

quote: { value: 'irritation', label: 'Irritation (ISO 10993-10)' },
error: Irritation testing moved out of ISO 10993-10 into ISO 10993-23:2021. ISO 10993-10:2021 covers skin sensitization only.
correct: Irritation (ISO 10993-23)

quote: { value: 'astm_f2346', label: 'ASTM F2346 — Vascular Stents' },
error: ASTM F2346 is the standard test method for static and dynamic characterization of spinal artificial discs, not vascular stents.
correct: Vascular stent standards include ASTM F2477 (pulsatile durability), ASTM F2079, ASTM F2081 and ISO 25539-2. F2346 is spinal artificial discs.

quote: Clinical data demonstrating reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness is the cornerstone of the PMA application per 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(v)(A).
error: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(v)(A) is the summary of nonclinical laboratory studies. The clinical investigations summary is (b)(3)(v)(B), and the full clinical section is 814.20(b)(6)(ii).
correct: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(v)(B) (clinical summary) and 814.20(b)(6)(ii) (results of clinical investigations).

quote: Software validation is required for all PMA devices containing software per IEC 62304 and 21 CFR 820.30(g).
error: 21 CFR 820.30(g) was removed by the QMSR on 2026-02-02. It is also the reference at line 1283.
correct: Design validation, including software validation, comes from ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3.7 through 21 CFR 820.10.

quote: Under Section 524B of the FD&C Act (enacted via PATCH Act), cybersecurity documentation is now a statutory requirement for premarket submissions.
error: Section 524B was enacted by section 3305 of FDORA in the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023. The PATCH Act was a bill that was never enacted itself. Also, 524B applies only to 'cyber devices', not to all premarket submissions. Separately, the 2023 guidance cited here as current ('Quality System Considerations') was superseded by FDA's final guidance of June 2025, 'Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions'.
correct: Section 524B (added by FDORA section 3305, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023) applies to cyber devices. The current guidance is the June 2025 'Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality Management System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions'.

quote: Post-market surveillance is a regulatory requirement for all PMA devices per 21 CFR 814.82.
error: 21 CFR 814.82 lists post-approval requirements FDA *may* impose in the approval order. It does not create a postmarket surveillance requirement for every PMA device. Section 522 postmarket surveillance orders fall under 21 CFR 822.
correct: Under 21 CFR 814.82, FDA may impose post-approval requirements (e.g. PAS, restrictions) as conditions of approval. Section 522 postmarket surveillance (21 CFR 822) applies only when FDA orders it. Every PMA holder must submit periodic reports (814.84) and MDRs (803).

quote: Per 21 CFR 820.198 — procedures for receiving, reviewing, and evaluating complaints
error: 21 CFR 820.198 was removed by the QMSR effective 2026-02-02.
correct: Complaint handling comes from ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.2.2 through 21 CFR 820.10, with the FDA-specific complaint record requirements in 21 CFR 820.35 (QMSR).

quote: Real-Time supplements (minor changes), or 30-day notices (editorial/minor changes).
error: A 30-day notice under 21 CFR 814.39(f) is for changes to manufacturing procedures or methods that affect safety or effectiveness, not for editorial changes. Changes that do not affect safety or effectiveness are reported in the annual report (814.39(b)). The list also leaves out the Special PMA supplement (changes being effected) under 814.39(d).
correct: 30-day notice / 135-day supplement (814.39(f)) covers manufacturing method or procedure changes. Editorial and other changes that do not affect safety or effectiveness go in the periodic (annual) report.

quote: Formal change control process per 21 CFR 820.30(i) for evaluating and documenting all device changes
error: 21 CFR 820.30(i) was removed by the QMSR effective 2026-02-02.
correct: Design change control comes from ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3.9 through 21 CFR 820.10.

quote: FDA conducts biennial inspections of PMA device manufacturers
error: The statutory biennial inspection requirement for Class II/III device establishments (FD&C Act 510(h)) was replaced by a risk-based inspection schedule under FDASIA (2012).
correct: FDA inspects device establishments on a risk-based schedule under FD&C Act section 510(h) as amended by FDASIA. There is no fixed biennial frequency.

quote: A Research (Investigator) IND (21 CFR 312.2(b)) is filed by a physician who both initiates and conducts the study.
error: 21 CFR 312.2(b) is the set of exemptions from the IND requirement (e.g., lawfully marketed drugs). It does not establish the investigator/research IND. The same wrong citation appears in the option description on line 167.
correct: The sponsor-investigator is defined in 21 CFR 312.3(b). An investigator IND is subject to the same content requirements in 312.23.

quote: { value: 'fast_track', label: 'Fast Track (21 CFR 312.300)'
error: 21 CFR 312.300 is the general provision of Subpart I, Expanded Access to Investigational Drugs for Treatment Use. It has nothing to do with Fast Track designation.
correct: Fast Track designation is under FD&C Act section 506(b) (21 USC 356(b)). The related regulations are 21 CFR 312 Subpart E (312.80-312.88).

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(a), the IND chemistry section must describe the drug product including its components, composition, and manufacturing.
error: 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(a) covers the drug substance. The drug product (components, quantitative composition, manufacturing) is (a)(7)(iv)(b). Line 1353 cites (iv)(a) for drug product composition with the same error.
correct: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(b) covers the drug product.

quote: Per 21 CFR Parts 210 and 211, all clinical trial material must be manufactured under current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP).
error: Since the 2008 final rule, 21 CFR 210.2(c) exempts most Phase 1 investigational drugs from Part 211. They are made under the statutory cGMP requirement and the 2008 Phase 1 CGMP guidance, not Part 211. Lines 425 and 499 repeat the claim that all clinical supplies must comply with Parts 210/211.
correct: Phase 1 investigational drugs are exempt from 21 CFR Part 211 (210.2(c)) but still need cGMP under FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B), following the guidance 'CGMP for Phase 1 Investigational Drugs' (2008). Part 211 applies from Phase 2 onward.

quote: A manufacturing site without recent FDA inspection history may face a pre-approval inspection (PAI), which can delay clinical supply release.
error: Pre-approval inspections under CPGM 7346.832 are done for marketing applications (NDA/ANDA/BLA), not INDs. A PAI does not gate the release of clinical supply. Line 479 also attributes PAIs to 21 CFR 211.
correct: PAIs happen during NDA/BLA review (CPGM 7346.832). FDA does not routinely inspect before an IND and does not use a PAI to gate clinical supply.

quote: reference: 'FDA Guidance: Immunogenicity Testing of Therapeutic Protein Products (2014); ICH S6(R1)',
error: The 2014 FDA guidance is 'Immunogenicity Assessment for Therapeutic Protein Products'. 'Immunogenicity Testing of Therapeutic Protein Products — Developing and Validating Assays for Anti-Drug Antibody Detection' was finalized in January 2019. The title and date are mismatched here and on line 587.
correct: Immunogenicity Assessment for Therapeutic Protein Products (August 2014), and/or Immunogenicity Testing of Therapeutic Protein Products — Developing and Validating Assays for ADA Detection (January 2019).

quote: Absence of GLP tox data will result in a clinical hold per 21 CFR 312.42(b)(1)(ii).
error: 312.42(b)(1)(ii) is the hold ground for clinical investigators who are not qualified by scientific training and experience. It is not about missing nonclinical data.
correct: The hold grounds that apply are 312.42(b)(1)(i), unreasonable and significant risk, and (b)(1)(iv), insufficient information to assess risks.

quote: The ICH S2(R1) standard genotoxicity battery must be completed before first-in-human dosing.
error: ICH M3(R2) says an in vitro gene mutation (Ames) assay is generally enough to support single-dose clinical trials, plus chromosomal damage assessment for multiple-dose trials. The complete standard battery is required before Phase 2, not before FIH.
correct: Per ICH M3(R2), the in vitro bacterial mutation assay (plus chromosomal damage assessment for multiple dosing) comes before FIH. The full S2(R1) battery must be complete before Phase 2.

quote: reference: 'ICH S2(R1); ICH M3(R2) Section 8',
error: Genotoxicity studies are not Section 8 of ICH M3(R2). Section 8 covers local tolerance studies.
correct: Genotoxicity studies are ICH M3(R2) Section 9.

quote: The IB should be updated at least annually (21 CFR 312.55(a)) and whenever significant new information becomes available.
error: 21 CFR 312.55(a) only requires the sponsor to give each investigator the IB before the investigation begins. The at-least-annual IB review is an ICH E6 GCP expectation, not a 312.55(a) requirement.
correct: 312.55(a) requires giving the IB to investigators. 312.55(b) requires keeping investigators informed of new observations. Annual IB review comes from ICH E6(R3), not 21 CFR.

quote: The PI must be qualified by training and experience as an appropriate expert per 21 CFR 312.53(c)(1).
error: 312.53(c)(1) describes the contents of Form FDA 1572. The requirement to select investigators qualified by training and experience is in 312.53(a).
correct: 21 CFR 312.53(a) covers selecting qualified investigators.

quote: The sponsor must also notify all participating investigators per 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1)(iii). Annual reports are due per 21 CFR 312.33 within 60 days of the IND anniversary date. Per ICH E2A, the sponsor must maintain a Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) framework.
error: 312.32(c)(1)(iii) is the category for reporting findings from animal or in vitro testing. The duty to notify FDA and all participating investigators sits in the lead-in of 312.32(c)(1). Also, the DSUR is defined by ICH E2F, not ICH E2A (E2A covers expedited reporting definitions and standards).
correct: Investigator notification comes from 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1). The DSUR is defined by ICH E2F.

quote: within 15 calendar days of initial receipt (7 days for fatal or life-threatening events)
error: Under 312.32(c)(1), the 15-day clock starts when the sponsor determines the information qualifies for reporting, not at initial receipt. Only the 7-day fatal or life-threatening clock (312.32(c)(2)) runs from the sponsor's initial receipt.
correct: 15 calendar days after the sponsor determines the information qualifies. 7 calendar days after initial receipt for unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reactions.

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.32: 7 calendar days for fatal/life-threatening SUSARs (with 8-day follow-up)
error: 21 CFR 312.32 has no 8-day follow-up requirement. The 8-day follow-up comes from ICH E2A / EU CT-3 practice. Under 312.32(d), follow-up information is submitted without delay, no later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor receives it.
correct: Follow-up IND safety reports under 312.32(d)(2) go in as soon as the information is available, and no later than 15 calendar days after receipt.

quote: The FDA IND Annual Report (21 CFR 312.33) is separately required and due within 60 days of the IND anniversary.
error: FDA accepts a DSUR prepared per ICH E2F in place of the 312.33 annual report, so the two are not both required.
correct: A DSUR may be submitted in lieu of the 312.33 IND annual report, within 60 days of the IND anniversary.

quote: A Special Protocol Assessment (SPA, 21 CFR 312.82 and FDA Guidance 2018) adds 45 days of FDA review for protocol agreement.
error: 21 CFR 312.82 covers early consultation (pre-IND and end-of-phase-1 meetings) for drugs treating life-threatening illnesses. SPA comes from FD&C Act 505(b)(5)(B)-(C). The same wrong citation appears on lines 1205 and 1254.
correct: The SPA authority is FD&C Act section 505(b)(5)(B) (21 USC 355(b)(5)(B)), with the FDA guidance 'Special Protocol Assessment' (Rev. 2, 2018).

quote: REMS evaluation is required per 21 USC 355-1 (FDAAA Section 505-1).
error: There is no requirement to evaluate REMS for an IND. 505-1 lets FDA require a REMS for NDA/BLA products. Also, 505-1 is a section of the FD&C Act (added by FDAAA section 901), not 'FDAAA Section 505-1'.
correct: FD&C Act section 505-1 (21 USC 355-1) lets FDA require a REMS for an approved or pending NDA/BLA. A REMS evaluation is not an IND requirement.

quote: { value: 'categorical_exclusion', label: 'Categorical Exclusion (21 CFR 25.31(a))', description: 'Most IND clinical investigations qualify' },
error: 21 CFR 25.31(a) excludes action on an NDA/ANDA/supplement that does not increase use of the active moiety. The categorical exclusion for an IND is 25.31(e). Lines 1217 and 1262 repeat 25.31(a).
correct: 21 CFR 25.31(e) is the categorical exclusion for action on an IND.

quote: Absence of any stability data may result in a Refuse to File or clinical hold.
error: Refuse to File (21 CFR 314.101 / 601.2) applies to NDAs and BLAs. FDA does not refuse to file an IND. INDs go into effect after 30 days or are placed on clinical hold.
correct: For an IND, missing stability data can lead to a clinical hold under 21 CFR 312.42. RTF does not apply.

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(ii), the IND must include a summary of the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of the drug, including ADME
error: 312.23(a)(7)(ii) says the amount of CMC information needed depends on the phase and scope of the investigation. It does not cover PK/PD. Animal ADME is under (a)(8)(i) and prior human PK under (a)(9).
correct: Animal pharmacology and ADME go under 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8)(i). Previous human experience, including PK, goes under 312.23(a)(9).

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Food-Effect Bioavailability and Fed Bioequivalence Studies" (2022)
error: The 2002 food-effect guidance was replaced in June 2022 by a differently titled guidance. No 2022 guidance carries the 2002 title. Line 1498 has the same confusion ('2002, revised 2022').
correct: FDA Guidance 'Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs — Clinical Pharmacology Considerations' (June 2022).

quote: Per FDA Guidance "In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies — Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions" (January 2020) and "Clinical Drug Interaction Studies — Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions" (January 2020)
error: Both January 2020 FDA DDI guidances were superseded and withdrawn when FDA adopted ICH M12 'Drug Interaction Studies' as final guidance in August 2024. They are still cited as current here and in the references on lines 1561, 1596, 1630-1631 and 1639-1640.
correct: ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies (FDA final guidance, August 2024).

quote: Per ICH E14 "Clinical Evaluation of QT/QTc Interval Prolongation and Proarrhythmic Potential for Non-Antiarrhythmic Drugs" (R3, 2015)
error: The ICH E14 guideline itself has no R3 revision. 'R3 (2015)' is the revision of the E14 Questions & Answers document. The E14/S7B Q&As followed in 2022.
correct: ICH E14 (2005), with the E14 Q&A (R3, 2015) and the E14/S7B Q&As (2022).

quote: All below ICH Q3A reporting threshold (0.10%) except Impurity A — identified and qualified.
error: Under ICH Q3A(R2), the reporting threshold for a maximum daily dose of 2 g or less is 0.05%. 0.10% is the identification threshold. The example contradicts the file's own help text on line 1804.
correct: Q3A(R2), max daily dose of 2 g or less: reporting threshold 0.05%, identification threshold 0.10%, qualification threshold 0.15%.

quote: label: 'Residual Solvents Assessed per ICH Q3C(R8)?',
error: ICH Q3C(R8) is superseded. Q3C(R9) reached Step 4 in January 2024. Line 1810 repeats R8.
correct: ICH Q3C(R9).

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Control of Nitrosamine Impurities in Human Drugs" (2021)
error: The February 2021 revision (Rev. 1) is superseded. FDA issued Revision 2 in September 2024. Line 1843 also cites the February 2021 version as current.
correct: FDA Guidance 'Control of Nitrosamine Impurities in Human Drugs' (Rev. 2, September 2024).

quote: sponsors of new drugs and biologics must submit an initial Pediatric Study Plan (iPSP) no later than 60 days after the End-of-Phase 2 (EOP2) meeting request or at an equivalent timepoint. Orphan-designated drugs are exempt from PREA.
error: Two errors. First, under 21 USC 355c(e) the iPSP is due within 60 calendar days after the EOP2 meeting itself, not the meeting request. Second, the orphan exemption is not absolute: FDARA 2017 (effective August 18, 2020) removed it for molecularly targeted oncology drugs under 505B(a)(3). The same unqualified orphan exemption appears on lines 1866-1867.
correct: The iPSP is due no later than 60 calendar days after the EOP2 meeting, or at a time agreed with FDA. Orphan-designated indications are exempt from PREA except molecularly targeted cancer drugs subject to 505B(a)(3).

quote: Reproductive and developmental toxicology per ICH S5(R3) must be completed before enrolling women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) in clinical trials.
error: ICH M3(R2) section 11 allows WOCBP into carefully monitored early trials before embryo-fetal development studies are done, if pregnancy risk is controlled (testing and highly effective contraception). In the US, definitive EFD studies are expected before Phase 3. The file's own text on line 1969 concedes this.
correct: Per ICH M3(R2), WOCBP can be enrolled in early trials before EFD studies if pregnancy-prevention precautions are in place. EFD studies are generally needed before Phase 3 or before larger or longer trials without such controls.

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Evaluation of Sex-Specific Data in Medical Device Clinical Studies" and ICH E1/E7
error: The cited FDA guidance covers medical devices (CDRH/CBER) and does not apply to a drug IND's PK/PD sex analysis. ICH E1 covers the extent of population exposure for chronic-use drugs, not sex differences.
correct: For drugs: the FDA Guideline for the Study and Evaluation of Gender Differences in the Clinical Evaluation of Drugs (1993), and 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(v) for NDA subgroup analyses.

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(a)(4), list sections with substantive labeling changes within the past year.
error: 201.57(a)(4) is the Highlights boxed warning. Recent Major Changes is 201.57(a)(5).
correct: Per 21 CFR 201.57(a)(5), list sections with recent major changes made within the past year.

quote: Standard PLR numbering is strongly recommended per 21 CFR 201.57(d).
error: PLR section and subsection numbering is required, not just recommended: 21 CFR 201.56(d)(1)-(2) mandate the numbered headings and order. 201.57(d) covers format requirements such as font size and highlighting, not numbering.
correct: Standard PLR section/subsection numbering is required per 21 CFR 201.56(d).

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(12), the Clinical Pharmacology section must include
error: 201.57(c)(12) covers the Description section (FPI section 11). Clinical Pharmacology is 201.57(c)(13).
correct: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(13), the Clinical Pharmacology section (12.1 Mechanism of Action, 12.2 Pharmacodynamics, 12.3 Pharmacokinetics)...

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(7), the Drug Interactions section must describe clinically significant interactions.
error: 201.57(c)(7) covers Adverse Reactions (FPI section 6). Drug Interactions (FPI section 7) is 201.57(c)(8).
correct: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(8), the Drug Interactions section...

quote: Reference FDA DDI guidance (2020) for study expectations.
error: The 2020 FDA in vitro and clinical DDI guidances were withdrawn and replaced when FDA adopted ICH M12 (Drug Interaction Studies), final in August 2024. Citing the 2020 guidance as current is out of date.
correct: Reference ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies (FDA final guidance, August 2024) for study expectations.

quote: reference: 'FDA Guidance: In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies — Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions (January 2020)'
error: This guidance was superseded by ICH M12 (FDA final guidance, August 2024), which replaced both the 2020 in vitro and the 2020 clinical DDI guidances.
correct: ICH M12: Drug Interaction Studies (FDA final guidance, August 2024)

quote: 8.1 Pregnancy (including lactation risk summary and data), 8.2 Lactation
error: Under PLLR, 8.1 Pregnancy does not contain the lactation risk summary. Lactation (its risk summary, clinical considerations and data) is its own subsection, 8.2. The parenthetical contradicts the next item.
correct: 8.1 Pregnancy (pregnancy exposure registry, risk summary, clinical considerations, data), 8.2 Lactation (risk summary, clinical considerations, data)

quote: UDI is required for all devices except certain exemptions (21 CFR 830.30).
error: 21 CFR 830.30 does not exist. The UDI labeling exceptions are in 21 CFR 801.30. The labeling requirement itself is 801.20, and Part 830 covers the UDI system, issuing agencies and GUDID.
correct: UDI is required on device labels per 21 CFR 801.20, except as provided in 21 CFR 801.30 (general exceptions).

quote: Per 21 CFR 801.15(c)(2), if symbols are used without adjacent explanatory text, a glossary must be included in the labeling or available via a toll-free number or website.
error: The stand-alone symbol glossary provision is in 801.15(c)(1)(i). 801.15(c)(2) concerns foreign-language representations. The rule requires a paper or electronic symbols glossary included in the labeling, plus a prominent statement saying where it is. A toll-free number is not a permitted way to provide it.
correct: Per 21 CFR 801.15(c)(1)(i), stand-alone symbols must be explained in a paper or electronic symbols glossary included in the labeling, with a prominent statement identifying the glossary's location.

quote: reducing the need for de novo studies — but requires a right-of-reference or published literature
error: A 505(b)(2) application is defined by relying on investigations the applicant did not conduct and has no right of reference to, such as published literature or FDA's prior finding for a listed drug. If the applicant has a right of reference to all the data, the application is a 505(b)(1).
correct: 505(b)(2) applies when the applicant relies on studies it neither conducted nor has a right of reference to, such as published literature or FDA's finding of safety and/or effectiveness for a listed drug.

quote: PDUFA user fees (21 CFR 314.50(l)) must be paid before FDA will file the application.
error: 21 CFR 314.50(l) covers the format of an original application (archival, review and field copies), not user fees. User fees are set by FD&C Act section 736 (21 USC 379h), and section 736(e) is what makes an application incomplete until the fee is paid. The same wrong citation appears at lines 269, 288 and 289.
correct: Cite FD&C Act section 736 (21 USC 379h), including 736(e) on unpaid fees. Remove the 21 CFR 314.50(l) citation.

quote: Standard review: 10 months from receipt. Priority review: 6 months from receipt.
error: This flow is mainly for 505(b)(1) NME NDAs. Under the PDUFA 'Program', the goal date for an NME NDA is 10 months (standard) or 6 months (priority) from the 60-day filing date, so 12 or 8 months from receipt. The file also contradicts itself: lines 222 and 2243 say the clock runs from the filing date for every NDA, which is wrong for non-NME NDAs, where it runs from receipt.
correct: NME NDAs and original BLAs: 10 or 6 months from the 60-day filing date (12 or 8 months from receipt). Non-NME NDAs: 10 or 6 months from receipt.

quote: Proposed shelf life should not exceed twice the long-term data period or the accelerated data period, whichever is shorter.
error: This misstates the extrapolation limit in ICH Q1E/Q1A(R2). The cap is twice the long-term data period and no more than 12 months beyond it. The accelerated data period plays no part in the cap.
correct: Proposed shelf life may be up to twice the period covered by long-term data, but no more than 12 months beyond it, when the data support extrapolation (ICH Q1E).

quote: ICH S1B(R1) allows alternatives to the traditional 2-year rat bioassay (e.g., p53+/- transgenic mouse model or rasH2 model)
error: Under ICH S1B, the rasH2 and p53+/- transgenic models replace the second species, the 2-year mouse study, not the rat bioassay. What S1B(R1) adds is a weight-of-evidence approach that can justify omitting the 2-year rat study.
correct: The transgenic mouse models (rasH2, p53+/-) are an alternative to the 2-year mouse bioassay. S1B(R1)'s weight-of-evidence approach can support waiving the 2-year rat study.

quote: Pregnancy must be listed as a contraindication in labeling, and a Medication Guide is likely required.
error: A nonclinical teratogenicity signal does not require a pregnancy contraindication. Under PLR/PLLR, a contraindication is used only when the risk clearly outweighs any possible benefit. Most drugs with embryo-fetal toxicity carry a W&P 'Embryo-Fetal Toxicity' statement plus content in section 8.1/8.3, not a contraindication.
correct: Embryo-fetal toxicity is usually addressed in Warnings and Precautions and in sections 8.1 and 8.3. A contraindication is warranted only when the risk clearly outweighs any benefit (21 CFR 201.57(c)(5)).

quote: Per FDA Guidance "Food-Effect Bioavailability and Fed Bioequivalence Studies" (2022)
error: The guidance titled 'Food-Effect Bioavailability and Fed Bioequivalence Studies' dates from 2002. The 2022 guidance that replaced it for NDAs is 'Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs — Clinical Pharmacology Considerations' (June 2022). The string pairs the old title with the new date.
correct: FDA Guidance 'Assessing the Effects of Food on Drugs in INDs and NDAs — Clinical Pharmacology Considerations' (June 2022).

quote: Per FDA Guidance "In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies — Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions" (January 2020) and "Clinical Drug Interaction Studies" (January 2020)
error: These two January 2020 guidances were superseded by ICH M12 'Drug Interaction Studies', which FDA issued as final guidance in August 2024 and which replaced both. The 'Figures 1-7 decision trees of the 2020 guidance' and the references at lines 909-910 are therefore out of date.
correct: Cite ICH M12 'Drug Interaction Studies' (FDA final guidance, August 2024), which superseded both 2020 FDA DDI guidances.

quote: A confirmatory study demonstrating clinical benefit is required post-approval (21 CFR 314.530).
error: 21 CFR 314.530 covers withdrawal procedures for accelerated approval. The confirmatory-study requirement is in 21 CFR 314.510 (and FD&C 506(c), as amended by FDORA). The same wrong citation appears at lines 1918, 1953 and 1993.
correct: The confirmatory study requirement is in 21 CFR 314.510 and FD&C 506(c). Section 314.530 covers withdrawal of approval.

quote: ICH E1(A) "The Extent of Population Exposure to Assess Clinical Safety" provides additional guidance.
error: There is no separate ICH E1(A) document. 'E1A' is the former code of the same ICH E1 guideline. The issue checks at lines 1367, 1375 and 1376 also cite E1(A) as a distinct source.
correct: ICH E1 (formerly coded E1A) is a single guideline. Cite ICH E1 only.

quote: It should be structured per ICH E2C(R2) "Periodic Benefit-Risk Evaluation Report" format.
error: ICH E2C(R2) defines the PBRER, a periodic postmarketing report. It is not the format for the NDA Integrated Summary of Safety. The ISS follows 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a), CTD Module 2.7.4/5.3.5.3 (ICH M4E) and FDA's ISS guidance. Line 1387 also cites E2C(R2) as the basis for the NDA's AE analysis.
correct: Structure the ISS per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(a), ICH M4E (Module 2.7.4 and 5.3.5.3) and FDA guidance on integrated summaries. E2C(R2) applies to postmarketing PBRERs.

quote: condition: { field: 'exposure_duration_12mo', operator: 'lt', value: 300 },
error: This critical issue check fires below 300 patients at 12 months and its message (line 1375) cites ICH E1. ICH E1 recommends about 100 patients exposed for at least 1 year (300-600 is the 6-month figure). The check contradicts the file's own E1 statement at lines 1301 and 1328.
correct: The ICH E1 recommendation is about 100 patients with at least 12 months of exposure (and 300-600 for 6 months).

quote: Per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b), individual patient narratives for all deaths (and other serious or significant AEs) must be included in the NDA.
error: 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) is the 4-month (120-day) safety update requirement. The requirement for case report forms for patients who died or withdrew because of an adverse event is 21 CFR 314.50(f)(2). Narratives come from the CSRs under ICH E3, section 12.3.2.
correct: CRFs for deaths and AE dropouts are required by 21 CFR 314.50(f)(2). Patient narratives are part of the CSRs under ICH E3, section 12.3.2.

quote:
{ value: 'ectd_v4', label: 'eCTD v4.0 (ICH M8 — current standard)' },
              { value: 'ectd_v3', label: 'eCTD v3.2.2 (transitional)' },
error: FDA began accepting eCTD v4.0 on an optional basis for new applications in September 2024. eCTD v3.2.2 is still the standard FDA supports and accepts, and v4.0 has not been made mandatory. Calling v3.2.2 'transitional' and v4.0 'the current standard' reverses the current status.
correct: eCTD v3.2.2 is FDA's supported standard. eCTD v4.0 (ICH M8) has been accepted optionally for new applications since September 2024.

quote: reference: 'FDA eCTD Mandate (21 CFR 314.50(a)); ICH M8',
error: The eCTD requirement comes from FD&C Act section 745A(a) and FDA's guidance 'Providing Regulatory Submissions in Electronic Format — Certain Human Pharmaceutical Product Applications…'. It does not come from 21 CFR 314.50(a), which covers the application form. Line 1559 also cites 314.50(a) for the CTD structure.
correct: Cite FD&C Act section 745A(a) and the associated FDA electronic submissions guidance (eCTD).

quote: The FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) performs automated validation of eCTD submissions.
error: The ESG is a transport gateway only. It does not validate eCTD content. CDER and CBER apply the eCTD technical rejection and validation criteria after receipt. 'eSubmitter' (line 1637) is a separate FDA form tool, not the eCTD validator. Lines 1700 and 1724 repeat the claim.
correct: The ESG transmits submissions. eCTD technical validation is done by FDA (CDER/CBER) after receipt against the eCTD Validation Criteria, and sponsors pre-validate with their own validation software.

quote: FDA Guidance "Format and Content of Proposed Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS), REMS Assessments, and Proposed REMS Modifications" (2009)
error: The 2009 REMS format and content guidance was a draft that FDA withdrew. It was replaced by 'Format and Content of a REMS Document' (2017 draft, later final) and the REMS assessment and modification guidances.
correct: Cite FDA Guidance 'Format and Content of a REMS Document' and the current REMS assessment and modification guidances.

quote: This applies to NMEs with remaining patent life or marketing exclusivity.
error: BPCA pediatric exclusivity is not limited to new molecular entities. It attaches to any existing patent or non-patent exclusivity listed for the drug's active moiety, whether or not the drug is an NME.
correct: Pediatric exclusivity adds 6 months to existing patents and exclusivities for any drug (active moiety) that fulfills a Written Request. It is not limited to NMEs.

quote: A Pre-NDA meeting (Type B, per FDA Guidance "Formal Meetings" (2017))
error: The 2017 'Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products' was a draft. It was superseded by the final guidance of September 2023, which reflects the PDUFA VII meeting types. Line 2089 repeats the 2017 date.
correct: FDA Guidance 'Formal Meetings Between the FDA and Sponsors or Applicants of PDUFA Products' (final, September 2023).

quote: { value: 'orphan_7yr', label: '7-Year Orphan Drug Exclusivity (21 USC 360bb)' },
error: 21 USC 360bb (FD&C 526) covers orphan designation. Orphan drug exclusivity is in 21 USC 360cc (FD&C 527).
correct: 7-year orphan drug exclusivity is at 21 USC 360cc (FD&C Act section 527).

quote: Paragraph IV certifications trigger a 45-day notice to the patent holder and may result in patent litigation with a 30-month stay.
error: The timing is misstated. Under FD&C 505(b)(3) and 21 CFR 314.52, the applicant must send notice within 20 days after FDA acknowledges filing. The 45-day period is the time the patent owner or NDA holder has after receiving notice to sue and trigger the 30-month stay.
correct: Notice of a Paragraph IV certification must be given within 20 days of FDA's filing acknowledgment. A suit filed within 45 days of receipt of that notice triggers the 30-month stay.

quote: The field copy certification confirms that a complete copy of Section 11 (case report tabulations/forms for serious AEs and study dropouts) has been provided.
error: Under 21 CFR 314.50(l)(3), the field copy is a copy of the chemistry, manufacturing and controls (CMC) technical section, plus Form 356h and the summary, sent to the FDA district office. It is not the case report tabulations or forms. A field copy is also not needed for applications submitted electronically in eCTD. Line 2199 repeats the error.
correct: The field copy certification relates to the CMC technical section sent to the district office (21 CFR 314.50(l)(3)). It is not required for eCTD submissions.

quote: label: 'Categorical Exclusion (21 CFR 25.31(a))',
error: 21 CFR 25.31(a) applies only when approval will not increase use of the active moiety. That does not fit a new molecular entity NDA, which this flow targets. NME NDAs usually claim exclusion under 25.31(b), where the expected introduction concentration is below 1 ppb. Line 2167 makes the same claim.
correct: NME NDAs usually claim categorical exclusion under 21 CFR 25.31(b) (EIC below 1 part per billion). Section 25.31(a) applies only when use of the active moiety does not increase.

quote: Companion diagnostic (CDx) NDA submitted in parallel to CDRH.
error: A companion diagnostic is a medical device. CDRH reviews it through a PMA, 510(k) or De Novo request, not through an NDA.
correct: Companion diagnostic PMA (or 510(k)/De Novo) submitted in parallel to CDRH.

quote: placeholder: 'e.g., QAS (Class II, Cardiovascular)',
error: Product code QAS is radiological computer-assisted triage and notification software (21 CFR 892.2080), reviewed by the Radiology panel, not the Cardiovascular panel.
correct: QAS is Class II, Radiology (892.2080). Either use a cardiovascular product code or label QAS as Radiology.

quote: For EMA submissions, the EudraCT number is required per Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 (Clinical Trials Regulation).
error: EudraCT numbers belonged to the old Directive 2001/20/EC regime. Under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, trials get an EU trial number through CTIS, and since 31 January 2025 every ongoing trial must have moved to the CTR. Also, CTAs go to Member States through CTIS, not to EMA.
correct: Under the CTR, an EU CT number is assigned in CTIS when the application is submitted to the Member States concerned.

quote: Required per 21 CFR 312.23 before shipping investigational product in the US.
error: 21 CFR 312.23 sets out IND content and format. The rule that an IND must be in effect before an investigational drug is shipped is in 21 CFR 312.40 (with 312.20).
correct: 21 CFR 312.40(a)-(b) (and 312.20): an IND must be in effect before shipment or clinical use.

quote: FDA generally requires concurrent controls for confirmatory trials per ICH E10 Section 2.1.4.
error: ICH E10 Section 2.1 covers placebo concurrent controls. External (including historical) controls are covered in Section 2.5.
correct: ICH E10 Section 2.5: External Control (Including Historical).

quote: reference: 'ICH E10 Section 2.1.4 — Choice of Control Group',
error: Wrong section. Historical/external controls are in ICH E10 Section 2.5, and Section 2.1 covers placebo concurrent controls.
correct: ICH E10 Section 2.5 — External Control (Including Historical).

quote: FDA Adaptive Design Guidance (2019) Section IV.C recommends simulation studies to evaluate operating characteristics under various scenarios.
error: Section IV of the 2019 FDA Adaptive Designs guidance describes types of adaptive designs, and IV.C covers population adaptations/enrichment. Simulations in adaptive design planning are covered in Section V.A (Special Considerations).
correct: FDA Adaptive Designs for Clinical Trials of Drugs and Biologics (2019), Section V.A — Simulations in Adaptive Design Planning.

quote: ICH E1 recommends long-term safety follow-up based on indication and duration of treatment.
error: ICH E1 covers the extent of population exposure needed to assess safety for drugs taken long-term for non-life-threatening conditions (about 1500 subjects total, 300-600 for 6 months, 100 for 1 year). It says nothing on post-treatment follow-up duration.
correct: ICH E1 sets minimum exposure numbers and durations for chronically used drugs. It does not cover post-treatment follow-up.

quote: Per 21 CFR 50 Subparts B-D, additional protections are required for certain populations.
error: In 21 CFR Part 50, Subpart B is Informed Consent of Human Subjects (general, not a vulnerable-population subpart) and Subpart C is reserved. Only Subpart D (children) adds protections for a specific population. The B-C-D pattern for pregnant women, prisoners and children belongs to 45 CFR 46.
correct: 21 CFR 50 Subpart D gives additional safeguards for children. Protections for pregnant women, fetuses, neonates and prisoners are in 45 CFR 46 Subparts B and C (HHS-funded research).

quote: Per PREA (Pediatric Research Equity Act) and 21 CFR 314.55, sponsors must submit a PSP unless a waiver or deferral is granted.
error: The PSP/iPSP obligation comes from FD&C Act section 505B(e), not 21 CFR 314.55. Also, a waiver or deferral request is made inside the iPSP, so it does not replace submitting one.
correct: FD&C Act 505B(e) requires an iPSP (which may include requested waivers or deferrals) within 60 days of the EOP2 meeting.

quote: Per 21 CFR 809.30, a companion diagnostic may be required if the drug is safe and effective only in patients identified by the diagnostic.
error: 21 CFR 809.30 covers restrictions on the sale, distribution and use of analyte specific reagents. It does not cover companion diagnostics. Companion diagnostic policy comes from the 2014 FDA guidance on In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices and the device premarket rules (PMA/510(k)/De Novo).
correct: Cite the FDA Guidance 'In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices' (2014) and the device premarket requirements (21 CFR Part 814 / 807 Subpart E). Do not cite 809.30.

quote: 'FDA Guidance: In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices (2014); 21 CFR 809.30'
error: 21 CFR 809.30 is the analyte specific reagent restriction. It is not a companion diagnostic provision.
correct: FDA Guidance: In Vitro Companion Diagnostic Devices (2014). Drop 21 CFR 809.30.

quote: ICH E9(R1) Addendum requires sponsors to precisely define the estimand with four attributes: (1) treatment condition, (2) population, (3) variable, (4) population-level summary measure, and to specify how each intercurrent event is handled.
error: ICH E9(R1) gives the estimand five attributes, and handling of intercurrent events is one of them. It is not a separate add-on to four attributes.
correct: Five attributes: treatment, population, variable (endpoint), handling of intercurrent events, and population-level summary measure.

quote: ICH E9(R1) defines four strategies: Treatment Policy (include data regardless), Composite (incorporate event into variable), Hypothetical (estimate effect in absence of event), Principal Stratum
error: ICH E9(R1) defines five strategies for intercurrent events. The text leaves out the 'while on treatment' strategy.
correct: Five strategies: treatment policy, hypothetical, composite variable, while on treatment, and principal stratum.

quote: Per 21 CFR 314.42 and FDAAA (2007), FDA may require a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy
error: 21 CFR 314.42 does not exist. REMS authority comes from section 505-1 of the FD&C Act, added by FDAAA 2007, and has no CFR section of its own.
correct: FD&C Act section 505-1 (21 U.S.C. 355-1), added by FDAAA 2007 Title IX.

quote: PREA requires an initial Pediatric Study Plan (iPSP) per 21 CFR 314.55.
error: The iPSP requirement is in FD&C Act section 505B(e), added by FDASIA in 2012, and is due within 60 days of the End-of-Phase 2 meeting. 21 CFR 314.55 predates it, covers pediatric assessments, waivers and deferrals, and does not mention an iPSP.
correct: FD&C Act section 505B(e) (PREA as amended by FDASIA 2012): submit an iPSP within 60 days of the EOP2 meeting, or as otherwise agreed.

quote: Per 21 CFR 50.55, assent is typically required for children aged 7 and older who are capable of providing it.
error: 21 CFR 50.55 sets no age threshold. The IRB decides whether children can assent, taking into account their ages, maturity and psychological state. 'Age 7' is a common convention, not a regulatory requirement.
correct: Under 21 CFR 50.55(a)-(b), the IRB decides whether children are capable of assenting, considering age, maturity and psychological state. The regulation sets no age.

quote: 21 CFR 312.6 specifies labeling requirements for investigational drugs including: name/code, batch number, storage conditions, route of administration, "Caution: New Drug — Limited by Federal Law to Investigational Use," and expiration date.
error: 21 CFR 312.6 requires only the caution statement 'Caution: New Drug--Limited by Federal (or United States) law to investigational use' on the immediate package. It also bars false or misleading statements. It does not specify name/code, batch number, storage conditions, route or expiration date.
correct: 312.6(a) requires the caution statement and 312.6(b) prohibits false or misleading labeling. Other label content comes from 21 CFR 211 (e.g., 211.137 exemptions for investigational drugs) and sponsor practice.

quote: EU Annex 13 (now replaced by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569) provides additional labeling requirements for IMP used in EU countries.
error: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 sets GMP principles for IMPs. IMP labelling requirements under the Clinical Trials Regulation are in Annex VI of Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 (Articles 66-70).
correct: EU IMP labelling: Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, Chapter X and Annex VI. GMP for IMPs: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/1569 and the EC GMP guidelines for IMPs.

quote: FDA Guidance on Diversity Plans to Improve Enrollment of Participants from Underrepresented Populations (2024) requires sponsors of Phase 3 and pivotal trials to submit a Diversity Action Plan.
error: A guidance cannot impose a requirement, and the 2024 document was a draft ('Diversity Action Plans to Improve Enrollment ...', June 2024). Under FDORA section 3601 (FD&C Act 505(z)/520(g)(9)), the duty applies only to studies whose enrollment starts 180 days or more after FDA publishes the final guidance. The text presents the requirement as already in force under the guidance.
correct: FDORA section 3601 created the DAP requirement for Phase 3/pivotal drug studies and certain device studies. It takes effect for studies enrolling 180 days after the final DAP guidance is published. The June 2024 document was a draft.

quote: FDA Draft Guidance on Decentralized Clinical Trials for Drugs, Biological Products, and Devices (2024)
error: The draft with this title came out in May 2023. FDA finalized it in September 2024 as 'Conducting Clinical Trials With Decentralized Elements', so in 2024 it was a final guidance, not a draft.
correct: FDA Final Guidance: Conducting Clinical Trials With Decentralized Elements (September 2024).

quote: EMA requires SUSARs to be reported to EudraVigilance per Regulation (EC) No 726/2004.
error: For clinical trials, the duty for sponsors to report SUSARs to EudraVigilance comes from Regulation (EU) No 536/2014, Article 42 (database under Article 40). Regulation 726/2004 covers post-authorisation pharmacovigilance.
correct: Sponsors report SUSARs electronically to the EudraVigilance database under Regulation (EU) No 536/2014 Article 42, with timelines in Annex III.

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.32(c)(2), unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reactions require initial reporting within 7 calendar days, with follow-up within 8 additional days.
error: The 'follow-up within 8 additional days' rule comes from the pre-2010 IND safety rule and from the EU. Current 21 CFR 312.32(c)(2) sets only the 7-calendar-day report. Follow-up information goes in as a follow-up IND safety report under 312.32(d)(2), as soon as it is available and no later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor receives it.
correct: 312.32(c)(2): report to FDA as soon as possible and no later than 7 calendar days after the sponsor first receives the information. Relevant follow-up goes under 312.32(d)(2), within 15 calendar days of receiving it.

quote: Per 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1), all other SUSARs require reporting within 15 calendar days of initial receipt.
error: Under 312.32(c)(1) the 15-day clock runs from when the sponsor determines that the information qualifies for reporting, not from initial receipt. The 7-day report in (c)(2) is the one that runs from initial receipt.
correct: No later than 15 calendar days after the sponsor determines the information qualifies for reporting.

quote: The DSUR is due within 60 days of the Development International Birth Date (DIBD).
error: Under ICH E2F the DSUR is due within 60 calendar days of its data lock point, which is the annual anniversary of the DIBD. It is not due within 60 days of the DIBD itself. ICH E2F also does not impose a submission duty on every authority: in the US the requirement is the 21 CFR 312.33 IND annual report, and a DSUR may be submitted in its place.
correct: Submit the DSUR within 60 days of the data lock point (the DIBD anniversary). In the US, a DSUR may replace the 312.33 annual report, which is due within 60 days of the anniversary of the IND going into effect.

quote: ICH E2F requires annual DSUR submission for all active INDs/CTAs.
error: FDA does not require a DSUR. US law requires an IND annual report under 21 CFR 312.33, and FDA accepts a DSUR in its place. An ICH guideline does not by itself impose a legal submission requirement on INDs.
correct: For INDs, 21 CFR 312.33 requires an annual report within 60 days of the IND effective-date anniversary, and an E2F DSUR may be submitted instead. In the EU, the CTR (Art. 43) requires an annual safety report (the DSUR).

quote: FDA may require REMS per 21 CFR 314.42.
error: 21 CFR 314.42 does not exist. REMS authority is FD&C Act section 505-1.
correct: FDA may require a REMS under FD&C Act section 505-1.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Section 4.1 requires top management to ensure that adequate resources are provided for the risk management process.
error: Clause 4.1 is the risk management process. Top management's duty to provide adequate resources is clause 4.2 (Management responsibilities).
correct: ISO 14971:2019 clause 4.2 requires top management to ensure adequate resources and competent personnel are assigned for risk management.

quote: label: 'SaMD Classification (IMDRF)', ... { value: 'class_a', label: 'Class A' }, { value: 'class_b', label: 'Class B' }, { value: 'class_c', label: 'Class C' }
