error: The IMDRF SaMD risk categorization framework (N12) uses Categories I, II, III and IV. Class A/B/C is the IEC 62304 software safety classification, not an IMDRF SaMD classification.
correct: IMDRF SaMD Category I / II / III / IV (or, if software safety class is intended, label it 'IEC 62304 Software Safety Class A/B/C').

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Section 7.3 requires verification that each risk control measure has been implemented in the final design and is effective in reducing risk.
error: Verifying the implementation and effectiveness of risk control measures is clause 7.2 (Implementation of risk control measures). Clause 7.3 is Residual risk evaluation.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 clause 7.2 requires verification of implementation and of effectiveness of each risk control measure.

quote: reference: 'ISO 14971:2019 Section 7.3',
error: The issue check is about unverified risk controls, which falls under clause 7.2, not 7.3 (Residual risk evaluation).
correct: ISO 14971:2019 clause 7.2

quote: reference: 'ISO 14971:2019 Section 7.3',
error: The issue check is about documenting verification evidence for controls. That is clause 7.2, with results recorded in the risk management file (4.5), not 7.3.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 clause 7.2 (and 4.5 risk management file)

quote: reference: 'ISO 14971:2019 Section 3, ISO/TR 24971:2020',
error: ISO 14971:2019 clause 3 is Terms and definitions. The risk management file requirement is clause 4.5.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 clause 4.5 (Risk management file); ISO/TR 24971:2020

quote: The narrative must include cause of death, contributing factors, autopsy findings (if available), and an independent sponsor assessment of causality.
error: ICH E3 §12.3.2 calls for 'brief narratives' that include the investigator's opinion on causality and the sponsor's opinion only 'if appropriate'. It does not make an independent sponsor causality assessment a required part of each death narrative.
correct: Per ICH E3 §12.3.2, each death gets a narrative that includes the investigator's causality opinion and, where appropriate, the sponsor's opinion.

quote: Per ICH E3 Section 12.3.1, the patient context is essential for causality assessment.
error: ICH E3 §12.3.1 is the listing of deaths, other serious adverse events and other significant adverse events. It is not the narratives section and does not cover patient context in narratives.
correct: Individual narratives are in ICH E3 §12.3.2 (Narratives of Deaths, Other Serious Adverse Events and Certain Other Significant Adverse Events).

quote: reference: 'ICH E2B(R3) Section B.1.7'
error: B.1.7 is the E2B(R2) data-element numbering for relevant medical history. E2B(R3) renumbered its elements, so B.1.7 does not exist in E2B(R3).
correct: In E2B(R3), relevant medical history is section D.7 (D.7.1 structured medical history, D.7.2 text). Cite 'ICH E2B(R3) D.7', or cite 'E2B(R2) B.1.7' and mark it as the former numbering.

quote: reference: 'ICH E2B(R3) Section B.2.i.4'
error: B.2.i.x is E2B(R2) numbering for reaction/event elements, and in R2 B.2.i.4 is the reaction start date. E2B(R3) has no section B.2.i.4.
correct: In E2B(R3), reaction/event data is section E.i (start date E.i.4). Time to onset from drug start is in G.k.9.i.3.1.

quote: reference: 'FDA CIOMS Form Guidance'
error: No FDA guidance has this title. The CIOMS I form is published by CIOMS, not FDA. FDA's own forms are MedWatch 3500/3500A.
correct: Cite the CIOMS I form (CIOMS), or ICH E2B(R3) G.k.9.i.4 / ICH E2A for dechallenge and rechallenge information.

quote: reference: 'ICH E2B(R3) Section B.4'
error: B.4 is the E2B(R2) drug-information section. E2B(R3) has no section B.4.
correct: In E2B(R3), drug information is section G.k. Rechallenge/recurrence is G.k.9.i.4 ('Did reaction recur on re-administration?').

quote: All systems used for Part 11 records must be validated per GAMP 5 principles.
error: This presents GAMP 5 as a regulatory requirement. 21 CFR 11.10(a) requires validation but names no method. GAMP 5 is voluntary ISPE industry guidance.
correct: 21 CFR 11.10(a) requires systems to be validated for accuracy, reliability, consistent intended performance and the ability to detect invalid or altered records. GAMP 5 is one commonly used, non-mandatory approach.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.1 requires stability data on at least three primary batches for registration.
error: Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.1 is 'General'. Batch selection is Section 2.2.3 for the drug product and Section 2.1.3 for the drug substance. The same wrong citation appears at lines 176, 249, 250 and 259.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.3 (Selection of Batches, drug product) and Section 2.1.3 (drug substance)

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.2 requires that stability testing be conducted in the container closure system proposed for marketing.
error: Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.2 is 'Photostability Testing'. Container closure is Section 2.2.4 for the drug product and Section 2.1.4 for the drug substance. The same wrong citation appears at lines 271, 279 and 327.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.4 (Container Closure System, drug product) and Section 2.1.4 (drug substance)

quote: 30 +/- 2 C / 75% +/- 5% RH (Zone IVb per ICH Q1F)
error: ICH Q1F was withdrawn in 2006 and never defined a Zone IVb 30°C/75% RH condition; it recommended 30°C/65% RH for Zones III and IV. Zone IVb and its 30°C/75% RH long-term condition come from WHO TRS 953 Annex 2 (2009). The same misattribution to ICH Q1F appears at line 360 ('ASEAN countries per ICH Q1F') and at line 362, which also presents Q1F as currently defining conditions by zone.
correct: Zone IVb (30°C/75% RH) is defined by WHO TRS 953 Annex 2 (2009). ICH Q1F is withdrawn.

quote: This condition is required if significant change occurs during accelerated testing per ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.2. At minimum 12 months at the intermediate condition is expected when significant change is observed.
error: Two problems. First, the intermediate-condition trigger is in Section 2.2.7.1 (General case); Section 2.2.7.2 covers drug products in impermeable containers. Second, the guideline calls for a 12-month intermediate study, but the initial application needs only a minimum of 6 months of data from it. The same wrong section citation appears at lines 438-439.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.1: when significant change occurs at accelerated, test at the intermediate condition. The initial application should include at least 6 months of data from a 12-month intermediate study.

quote: EMA Guideline CPMP/QWP/609/96
error: CPMP/QWP/609/96 is the EMA guideline on declaration of storage conditions. The EMA note for guidance on in-use stability testing is CPMP/QWP/2934/99.
correct: Note for Guidance on In-Use Stability Testing of Human Medicinal Products (CPMP/QWP/2934/99)

quote: - Intermediate (if needed): 12 months minimum
error: This line lists minimum durations at the time of submission. For the intermediate condition, ICH Q1A(R2) requires 6 months of data at submission, from a 12-month study, not 12 months.
correct: Intermediate (if needed): at least 6 months of data at submission, from a 12-month study

quote: Standard testing intervals per ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.1
error: Testing frequency is Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.6 for the drug product and Section 2.1.6 for the drug substance. Section 2.2.7.1 covers storage conditions (General case).
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.6 / 2.1.6 (Testing Frequency)

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.4 requires that testing should cover those features susceptible to change during storage
error: Section 2.2.4 is 'Container Closure System'. The requirement to test attributes susceptible to change, using validated stability-indicating procedures, is in Section 2.2.5 (Specification) and Section 2.1.5 for the drug substance. The same wrong citation appears at lines 803 and 804.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.5 / 2.1.5 (Specification)

quote: ICH Q1E Section 3.1: Use ANCOVA to test equality of slopes and intercepts at alpha = 0.25.
error: ICH Q1E has no Section 3.1. Its main text is Sections 1-2, followed by Appendices A and B. The poolability test is in Appendix B (B.2.2.1), and extrapolation is in Section 2.3. The same nonexistent sections are cited at line 968 ('ICH Q1E Section 3') and at lines 980, 1046 and 1047 ('ICH Q1E Section 4').
correct: Poolability testing: ICH Q1E Appendix B (B.2.2.1). Extrapolation: ICH Q1E Section 2.3 (with Sections 2.4-2.7 and Appendix A).

quote: For drug substances, a retest period rather than an expiration date is assigned per ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.4.
error: Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.4 is 'Container Closure System'. Retest period assignment is covered in Section 2.1.9 (Evaluation) and in the Glossary.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.9 (Evaluation) and the Glossary definition of retest period

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.2 (drug substances) and Section 2.2.3 (drug products) describe stress testing requirements.
error: Section 2.2.3 is 'Selection of Batches' for the drug product. Q1A(R2) has no drug product stress testing section; stress testing is Section 2.1.2, for the drug substance only. The same wrong citation appears at lines 1122 and 1123.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.2 (Stress Testing, drug substance). Drug product photostability is Section 2.2.2 and ICH Q1B.

quote: expects the post-approval stability protocol to be described in CTD Module 3.2.P.8.3 (drug product) or 3.2.S.7.3 (drug substance)
error: In the CTD (ICH M4Q), 3.2.P.8.3 and 3.2.S.7.3 hold the Stability Data. The post-approval stability protocol and commitment belong in 3.2.P.8.2 and 3.2.S.7.2.
correct: CTD 3.2.P.8.2 / 3.2.S.7.2 (Post-approval Stability Protocol and Stability Commitment)

quote: A comparability protocol (21 CFR 314.70(a))
error: 21 CFR 314.70(a) sets out the general requirements for supplements. Comparability protocols are covered in 21 CFR 314.70(e).
correct: 21 CFR 314.70(e) (601.12(e) for biologics)

quote: EMA requires notification of quality defects under Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161.
error: Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/161 covers the safety features on packaging (unique identifier and anti-tampering device) under the Falsified Medicines Directive. It is not the legal basis for reporting quality defects.
correct: In the EU, quality defects are reported under Directive 2001/83/EC (Art. 23 and Art. 117), Commission Directive (EU) 2017/1572 (GMP) and EU GMP Chapter 8.

quote: Per FDA Process Validation Guidance (2011), Stage 2 (Process Qualification) must be completed at commercial scale, typically with a minimum of three consecutive successful batches
error: The 2011 FDA Process Validation guidance deliberately dropped the three-batch convention. It sets no minimum number of PPQ batches; the number must be justified scientifically. Line 508 attributes the same three-batch minimum to the guidance.
correct: The 2011 guidance sets no minimum batch number. The number of PPQ batches must be justified by risk and process understanding.

quote: Form FDA 356h (Application to Market a New Drug, Biologic, or Antibiotic Drug for Human Use)
error: This is the obsolete form title. Antibiotics have not been a separate application class since FDAMA 1997, and the current form is titled differently.
correct: Form FDA 356h, 'Application to Market a New or Abbreviated New Drug or Biologic for Human Use'.

quote: Orphan products may qualify for a fee waiver under 21 USC 360bb.
error: 21 USC 360bb (FD&C 526) is orphan designation. The exemption from the PDUFA application fee for orphan-only applications is in 21 USC 379h(a)(1)(F) (FD&C 736(a)(1)(F)).
correct: Orphan application-fee exemption: 21 USC 379h(a)(1)(F), for an application whose only indications are orphan-designated.

quote: Foreign sponsors must also designate a US Agent per 21 CFR 600.4.
error: 21 CFR 600.4 does not exist and does not create a US-agent requirement. Part 600 Subpart A contains only 600.2 and 600.3.
correct: No 21 CFR 600.x US-agent provision exists. Cite the Form FDA 356h countersignature requirement instead.

quote: Products with significant CRS risk (e.g., CAR-T therapies, bispecific antibodies, T-cell engagers) typically require a REMS with ETASU per 21 USC 355-1.
error: In June 2025, FDA eliminated the REMS for the approved autologous CAR-T products (BCMA- and CD19-directed). CAR-T is therefore no longer an example of a product that 'typically requires' a REMS with ETASU.
correct: Since June 2025, the approved autologous CAR-T products have no REMS; CRS risk is managed through labeling (Boxed Warning). Whether a REMS is needed is decided product by product.

quote: FDA's Benefit-Risk Framework (2023) requires sponsors to present a structured assessment covering analysis of condition, current treatment options, benefit, risk, and risk management across the five key decision factors.
error: The Benefit-Risk Framework is FDA's own review tool, described in guidance (the 2023 draft guidance is non-binding). It does not require sponsors to present anything. It also has four dimensions, not five decision factors.
correct: FDA's Benefit-Risk Framework (four dimensions: Analysis of Condition, Current Treatment Options, Benefit, Risk and Risk Management) is used by FDA reviewers; the 2023 draft guidance recommends, and does not require, that sponsors present benefit-risk information this way.

quote: Include a structured benefit-risk table using FDA's five-factor framework: (1) Analysis of Condition, (2) Current Treatment Options, (3) Benefit, (4) Risk and Risk Management, (5) Summary Assessment.
error: FDA's framework has four dimensions. Its last element is the conclusions or summary that follows those dimensions, not a fifth factor. The text also contradicts the flow's own five-dimension list, which splits Risk and Risk Management.
correct: Four dimensions (Analysis of Condition, Current Treatment Options, Benefit, Risk and Risk Management) followed by a conclusions/summary row.

quote: FDA requires a 120-day safety update per 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) to ensure the Advisory Committee has access to the most recent safety data at the time of the meeting.
error: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) requires an NDA applicant to update its pending application with new safety information: 4 months after submission, after a complete response letter, and when FDA requests one. It does not concern an Advisory Committee and applies to NDAs, not BLAs. The supporting reference on line 115, 'Safety Reporting Requirements for INDs and BA/BE Studies (2012)', covers IND safety reporting under 21 CFR 312.32, not the NDA safety update. The question on line 104 also says the update is 'required by FDA guidance'; it is required by regulation.
correct: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) requires NDA safety updates to the pending application (4 months after submission, after a complete response letter, and on FDA request); it does not concern Advisory Committee materials.

quote: FDA Guidance: Evaluation of Sex-Specific Data (2020)
error: The FDA guidance is 'Evaluation of Sex-Specific Data in Medical Device Clinical Studies', issued in August 2014, not 2020, and it covers medical devices. It does not apply to an NDA/BLA advisory committee briefing.
correct: 'Evaluation of Sex-Specific Data in Medical Device Clinical Studies' (2014), which applies to devices only; for drugs, FDA's 'Guideline for the Study and Evaluation of Gender Differences in the Clinical Evaluation of Drugs' (1993).

quote: All data presented to the Advisory Committee must be consistent with the submitted application per 21 CFR Part 14.25 and FDA Advisory Committee Guidance.
error: 21 CFR 14.25 is 'Portions of advisory committee meetings'. It defines the open public hearing, open committee discussion and closed portions. It says nothing about data consistency with the application.
correct: 21 CFR 14.25 defines the portions of an advisory committee meeting; no Part 14 provision imposes a data-consistency requirement of this kind.

quote: derived from a clearly defined safety population per ICH E9 Section 5.6.
error: ICH E9 Section 5.6 is 'Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels' (multiplicity). The set of subjects for safety evaluation is covered in Section 6 (Evaluation of Safety and Tolerability), Section 6.3.
correct: ICH E9 Section 6.3 (Set of Subjects to be Evaluated and Presentation of Data) within Section 6, Evaluation of Safety and Tolerability.

quote: The sponsor's briefing document must address the specific questions identified by FDA for Advisory Committee discussion per 21 CFR 14.25(b).
error: 21 CFR 14.25 sets out the portions of an advisory committee meeting. Neither 14.25(b) nor any other Part 14 provision requires the sponsor's briefing document to address FDA's discussion questions.
correct: Addressing FDA's discussion questions is good practice; it is not a requirement of 21 CFR 14.25(b), which concerns the meeting's portions.

quote: Responder analyses are recommended per ICH E9 Section 5.4 and FDA Guidance
error: ICH E9 Section 5.4 is 'Data Transformation' (for example, log transformation). It does not recommend responder analyses.
correct: ICH E9 Section 5.4 covers data transformation; responder/dichotomized endpoints are not the subject of that section.

quote: FDA Guidance: Missing Data in Confirmatory Trials (2020)
error: FDA has issued no guidance of this title. The well-known documents are the National Research Council report 'The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials' (2010, commissioned by FDA) and the EMA 'Guideline on Missing Data in Confirmatory Clinical Trials' (2010). ICH E9(R1) (2019) now covers handling of intercurrent events and missing data.
correct: Cite ICH E9(R1) (2019), the NRC report (2010), or the EMA Guideline on Missing Data in Confirmatory Clinical Trials (EMA/CPMP/EWP/1776/99 Rev. 1, 2010).

quote: 'FDA Benefit-Risk Framework (2023); ICH E9 Section 5.4; FDA Advisory Committee Guidance (2008)'
error: ICH E9 Section 5.4 is 'Data Transformation'. It does not address NNT/NNH.
correct: Remove the ICH E9 Section 5.4 citation for NNT/NNH; that section covers data transformation.

quote: which exceeds the recommended 300-page limit
error: No FDA regulation or guidance sets a 300-page limit for sponsor Advisory Committee briefing documents. The finding presents an invented threshold as an FDA recommendation; line 544 repeats it as FDA Advisory Committee Guidance.
correct: FDA guidance does not set a page limit; any page threshold is an internal or industry heuristic and should be labeled as such.

quote: For Class III and implantable devices, EU MDR Article 61(4) requires clinical investigations unless reliance on equivalence or other clinical data can be duly justified per Article 61(10).
error: Article 61(10) is not an exception to the Article 61(4) clinical investigation requirement. It applies 'without prejudice to paragraph 4', and it covers cases where clinical data is not deemed appropriate and conformity rests on non-clinical data. The exceptions to 61(4) are in 61(4) itself (modifications), 61(5) (equivalence with a contract) and 61(6) (legacy/listed devices). Lines 174, 411, 414, 851 and 854 repeat the error.
correct: Article 61(4) exemptions: 61(4) second subparagraph, 61(5) and 61(6). Article 61(10) justification is not available for Class III/implantable devices in place of the clinical investigations 61(4) requires.

quote: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Sections 8 & Appendix A9
error: Appendix A9 is the proposed CER table of contents, not the literature search protocol. Section 8 is appraisal of pertinent data (Stage 2). Identifying data, including the literature search, is Section 7, and the search protocol elements are in Appendix A5. Line 345 makes the same A9 cite, and lines 226, 237, 266-267, 284, 311-312 and 770 cite Section 8 for the literature search.
correct: Literature search: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Section 7 (Stage 1, identification of pertinent data), with Appendix A4 (sources) and Appendix A5 (literature search and review protocol).

quote: Provide a GSPR checklist mapping relevant requirements (especially GSPRs 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 14, 22, 23) to the clinical evidence presented in the CER. Follow MDCG 2021-24 format.
error: MDCG 2021-24 is the guidance on classification of medical devices. It is not a GSPR checklist format (also cited at line 552).
correct: The GSPR checklist content follows MDR Annex II Section 4. MDCG 2021-24 is about classification under Annex VIII.

quote: EU MDR Annex I GSPR 2 requires that residual risks be deemed acceptable when weighed against clinical benefits and that they are communicated to users.
error: GSPR 2 requires reducing risks as far as possible without adversely affecting the benefit-risk ratio. Accepting the overall residual risk and informing users about residual risks is GSPR 4 (and GSPR 8 for side-effects). Lines 596 and 608 repeat the GSPR 2 cite.
correct: EU MDR Annex I Section 4: risk control measures, residual risk judged acceptable, and users informed of any residual risks. Section 2 is risk reduction as far as possible.

quote: For Class III and implantable devices, MDCG 2020-13 recommends at least annual updates; for lower classes, the interval should be justified.
error: MDCG 2020-13 is the Clinical Evaluation Assessment Report (CEAR) template for notified bodies. The 'at least annually' requirement for Class III/implantable devices is in MDR Article 61(11) itself, and it covers the PMCF evaluation report and SSCP, not a recommendation in MDCG 2020-13.
correct: MDR Article 61(11): for Class III and implantable devices, the PMCF evaluation report and, if indicated, the SSCP are updated at least annually with clinical data. MDCG 2020-13 is the CEAR template.

quote: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3 provides a hierarchy of evidence.
error: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 Appendix A3 is 'Device description - typical contents'. It contains no evidence hierarchy. Lines 680 and 692 repeat the cite.
correct: Appraisal of data quality is in Section 8 and Appendix A6 (studies lacking scientific validity). A3 is the device description.

quote: MEDDEV 2.7/1 Rev 4 requires the CER to contain: scope (Section 7), clinical background and state of the art (Section 9), literature search methodology (Section 8), clinical data appraisal (Section 8), analysis of clinical data (Section 9), and conclusions including benefit-risk (Section 10).
error: Rev 4's sections are mis-mapped. Scope/Stage 0 (including the device description) is Section 6, not 7. Identification of data and the literature search is Section 7, not 8. The same mis-mapping appears at lines 64, 93-94 and 768 (device description/classification as 'Section 7').
correct: Section 6: scope (Stage 0). Section 7: identification of pertinent data, including the literature search (Stage 1). Section 8: appraisal (Stage 2). Section 9: analysis (Stage 3). Section 10: the clinical evaluation report (Stage 4). The CER table of contents is Appendix A9.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7, including materials of construction, specifications, and compatibility data.
error: Q1A(R2) 2.2.7 is Storage Conditions. Container closure is 2.2.4. The same wrong citation is at line 115.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.4, Container Closure System.

quote: ICH Q6A Section 3.3 and Q7 Section 11.4 require a well-characterized primary reference standard
error: ICH Q7 Section 11.4 is Certificates of Analysis. Reference standards are covered at Q7 paragraphs 11.17-11.19, under 11.1 General Controls. ICH Q6A 3.3 is Specific Tests/Criteria; the Q6A reference standard concept is Section 2.11. The same wrong citations are at line 138.
correct: ICH Q7 paragraphs 11.17-11.19 (11.1 General Controls); ICH Q6A Section 2.11 (Reference Standard).

quote: ICH Q6A Section 4 requires that specifications be set based on manufacturing experience, stability data, and batch analysis results.
error: ICH Q6A Section 4 is the Glossary. Specification justification is in Section 3.1. The same wrong citation is at line 236.
correct: ICH Q6A Section 3.1, Specifications: Definition and Justification.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) mandates long-term (25C/60%RH), intermediate (30C/65%RH), and accelerated (40C/75%RH) stability studies
error: Q1A(R2) does not require intermediate studies in every case. They are needed only when long-term is 25°C/60% RH and significant change occurs at accelerated conditions. Long-term may also be 30°C/65% RH, in which case there is no intermediate condition.
correct: Long-term 25°C/60% RH or 30°C/65% RH plus accelerated 40°C/75% RH. Intermediate 30°C/65% RH applies only if significant change occurs at accelerated (Q1A(R2) 2.1.7/2.2.7.1).

quote: ICH Q3C(R8) establishes concentration limits for residual solvents
error: ICH Q3C(R8) is superseded by Q3C(R9) (Step 4, January 2024). The (R8) citation also appears at lines 286 and 355.
correct: ICH Q3C(R9).

quote: ICH Q8(R2) Section 2.1; ICH Q9; ICH Q10; ICH Q11 Section 5
error: ICH Q11 Section 5 is Selection of Starting Materials and Source Materials. It does not cover CQA identification.
correct: ICH Q11 Section 3 (Manufacturing Process Development, including 3.1.1 drug substance CQAs); ICH Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.2 (CQAs).

quote: FDA encourages supply chain resilience per the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) and FDA Drug Shortages guidance.
error: DSCSA covers product tracing and serialization (track-and-trace) of prescription drugs. It is not a framework for supply resilience or second-sourcing.
correct: Drug shortage and supply resilience obligations come from FDCA 506C (discontinuance/interruption notification) and FDASIA, with FDA's guidance on notifying FDA of a permanent discontinuance or interruption in manufacturing. DSCSA is traceability.

quote: ICH Q10 Section 3.2.4 and WHO TRS 961 Annex 7 recommend a structured technology transfer process
error: ICH Q10 3.2.4 is Management Review of Process Performance and Product Quality. Technology transfer is 3.1.2. The same wrong citation is at line 577.
correct: ICH Q10 Section 3.1.2, Technology Transfer.

quote: ICH Q10 Section 2; ICH Q8(R2) Section 4; ICH Q11 Section 9
error: ICH Q11 Section 9 is Lifecycle Management; control strategy is Q11 Section 6. ICH Q10 Section 2 is Management Responsibility, not the control strategy definition (line 693 says Q10 Section 2 describes control strategy).
correct: ICH Q11 Section 6 (Control Strategy); ICH Q8(R2) Part II Section 2.5 (Control Strategy); the Q10 definition is in its Glossary.

quote: 'ICH E3 Sections 2 and 6 require a clear statement of the primary study ' +
error: ICH E3 Section 6 is Investigators and Study Administrative Structure. Study objectives are in Section 8. Line 177 repeats the citation as 'ICH E3, Sections 2 & 6'.
correct: ICH E3 Section 2 (Synopsis) and Section 8 (Study Objectives).

quote: 'Per ICH E9 Section 5.3 and the NRC/FDA report on missing data (2010), a ' +
error: Neither ICH E9 Section 5.3 nor the 2010 NRC report sets a 20% discontinuation threshold. The figure is attributed to sources that do not contain it (see also line 244, 'the 20% threshold commonly flagged').
correct: No regulatory or ICH threshold exists. ICH E9 5.3 and the NRC report address minimizing missing data and analyzing its impact without a numeric cutoff, so 20% should be presented as an internal heuristic only.

quote: 'Per ICH E3 Section 12.2 and 21 CFR 312.32, the CSR must include a ' +
error: 21 CFR 312.32 governs expedited IND safety reporting (15-/7-day reports). It does not set CSR content requirements such as AE tabulation by SOC/PT. Line 469 repeats it as a reference.
correct: CSR AE tabulation comes from ICH E3 Section 12.2 (and 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5) for NDA content). 21 CFR 312.32 covers IND safety reports only.

quote: 'Every SAE and death must have an individual narrative per ICH E3 Section 12.3.3, ' +
error: In ICH E3, narratives of deaths, other serious AEs and other significant AEs are Section 12.3.2. Section 12.3.3 is Analysis and Discussion of these events. Line 502 cites '12.3.1 & 12.3.3' for the same requirement.
correct: ICH E3 Section 12.3.2 (Narratives of Deaths, Other Serious Adverse Events and Certain Other Significant Adverse Events); 12.3.1 is the listings.

quote: 'ICH E6(R3) principles; 21 CFR 312.120; ICH E3, Section 9.6; 21 CFR 50',
error: ICH E3 Section 9.6 is Data Quality Assurance. Ethics content (IEC/IRB, ethical conduct, patient information and consent) is Section 5. Also, 21 CFR 312.120 applies only to foreign clinical studies not conducted under an IND, not to every CSR, as the question at line 591 implies.
correct: ICH E3 Section 5 (5.1 IEC/IRB, 5.2 Ethical Conduct of the Study, 5.3 Patient Information and Consent). 21 CFR 312.120 applies only to foreign non-IND studies submitted in support of an IND or marketing application.

quote: 'FDA Guidance on Data Monitoring Committees (2006) and ICH E9 Section 4.5 ' +
error: In ICH E9, Section 4.5 is Interim Analysis and Early Stopping. The independent DMC is Section 4.6. Neither the guidance nor E9 'requires' a DMC charter: the 2006 FDA DMC guidance is non-binding and recommends one. The reference at line 636 repeats Section 4.5.
correct: ICH E9 Section 4.6 (Role of Independent Data Monitoring Committee). FDA's 2006 DMC guidance recommends, and does not require, a written charter.

quote: 'ICH E9, Section 4.5; FDA Guidance on DMCs (2006); ICH E3, Section 11.4.6',
error: ICH E3 Section 11.4.6 is By-Patient Displays. Interim analyses and data monitoring are in Section 11.4.2.3.
correct: ICH E3 Section 11.4.2.3 (Interim Analyses and Data Monitoring).

quote: 'ICH E9 Section 2.3 requires that any deviation from the pre-specified SAP be ' +
error: ICH E9 Section 2.3 is Design Techniques to Avoid Bias (blinding, randomisation). Pre-specification of the analysis and changes to it are in Section 5.1 (with 4.2 on changes made during the trial). Line 706 repeats 'ICH E9, Section 2.3'. ICH E3 11.4.1 (Analysis of Efficacy) is also not the place where changes to planned analyses are reported; that is E3 9.8.
correct: ICH E9 Section 5.1 (Prespecification of the Analysis); ICH E3 Section 9.8 (Changes in the Conduct of the Study or Planned Analyses).

quote: 'ICH E9, Section 5.7; FDA Guidance on Subgroup Analyses (2019)',
error: FDA has issued no 'Guidance on Subgroup Analyses (2019)'. The 2019 subgroup guideline is EMA's (Guideline on the investigation of subgroups in confirmatory clinical trials, EMA/CHMP/539146/2013).
correct: EMA Guideline on the investigation of subgroups in confirmatory clinical trials (EMA/CHMP/539146/2013, effective 2019), or ICH E9 Section 5.7.

quote: 'ICH E9, Section 5.2.3; ICH E9(R1) Addendum; ICH E3, Section 11.4.3',
error: ICH E3 Section 11.4.3 is Tabulation of Individual Response Data, not sensitivity analyses. Sensitivity and robustness analyses fall under Section 11.4.2 (Statistical/Analytical Issues).
correct: ICH E3 Section 11.4.2 (Statistical/Analytical Issues).

quote: 'ICH E3 Section 12.5 requires an integrated safety summary with conclusions ' +
error: ICH E3 Section 12.5 is Vital Signs, Physical Findings and Other Observations Related to Safety. Safety Conclusions is Section 12.6. Lines 874 and 909 repeat 'ICH E3, Section 12.5' as the safety-conclusions reference.
correct: ICH E3 Section 12.6 (Safety Conclusions).

quote: Under 21 CFR 807.87(b), the submitter must state the classification of the device (Class I, II, or III).
error: 807.87(b) is the establishment registration number. The device class, and the classification panel if known, is 807.87(c). The same wrong cite appears at lines 82, 85, 86, 115 (product code) and 144-145 (regulation number).
correct: 21 CFR 807.87(c): the class under Part 860 and, if known, its classification panel (or a statement that it has not been classified).

quote: ISO 10993-1:2018; FDA Guidance: Use of International Standard ISO 10993-1 — Biological Evaluation of Medical Devices (2020)
error: FDA revised the 2020 ISO 10993-1 guidance in September 2023, so the 2020 version is not current. pma-auditor.ts line 121 has the same issue.
correct: FDA Guidance: Use of International Standard ISO 10993-1, 'Biological evaluation of medical devices - Part 1' (September 2023 revision).

quote: If the device is a "cyber device" (contains software, connects to the internet, or has cybersecurity vulnerabilities)
error: FD&C Act 524B(c) defines a cyber device by three criteria that must all be met (AND), not any one (OR). The question at line 534 is also too broad: it says any device with software or network connectivity must provide an SBOM and threat modeling.
correct: A cyber device (1) includes software validated, installed or authorized by the sponsor as or in a device, AND (2) can connect to the internet, AND (3) has technological characteristics that could be vulnerable to cybersecurity threats.

quote: FDA Guidance: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices — Quality System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions (2023)
error: The September 2023 final guidance was superseded by a revised final guidance in June 2025. pma-auditor.ts lines 790-791 also cite the 2023 version.
correct: Cybersecurity in Medical Devices: Quality System Considerations and Content of Premarket Submissions (final, June 2025).

quote: ICH S2(R1) requires a standard battery of genotoxicity tests before Phase 1.
error: Under ICH M3(R2) Section 7, a gene mutation (Ames) assay is enough to support single-dose trials. A mammalian chromosomal damage assay is added before multiple-dose trials, and the complete battery is needed before Phase 2. Line 204's description of the battery as 'two mammalian cell assays' also misstates S2(R1). Option 1 is Ames plus one in vitro mammalian assay plus one in vivo assay. Option 2 is Ames plus an in vivo assessment in two tissues.
correct: Ames before single-dose FIH; a mammalian chromosomal damage assay added before multiple-dose trials; the complete S2(R1) battery (Option 1 or 2) before Phase 2 (ICH M3(R2) Section 7).

quote: Drug products for use in clinical investigations must be manufactured in compliance with CGMP per 21 CFR 211 and 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(b).
error: Most Phase 1 investigational drugs are exempt from Part 211 under 21 CFR 210.2(c). They are made under the FD&C Act 501(a)(2)(B) CGMP standard, following the 2008 Phase 1 CGMP guidance. 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(b) is the drug product description and imposes no CGMP requirement. Line 309 repeats the claim that Part 211 is required, and line 291 repeats the 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(b) claim.
correct: Phase 1 investigational drugs are exempt from Part 211 (21 CFR 210.2(c)) and follow statutory CGMP per the 2008 Phase 1 CGMP guidance. Part 211 applies from Phase 2 onward.

quote: Foreign sponsors must designate a US agent per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(v).
error: 312.23(a)(1)(v) is the commitment to follow all other applicable regulatory requirements. The requirement for a US-resident attorney, agent or official to countersign is in 312.23(a)(1)(ix).

quote: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(ix) requires a commitment to obtain IRB approval.
error: 312.23(a)(1)(ix) is the sponsor signature and US countersignature requirement. The IRB commitment is 312.23(a)(1)(iv). The question on line 450 makes the same error and also misstates the requirement as a 'statement that an IRB has been identified'.
correct: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(iv): a commitment that a Part 56-compliant IRB will be responsible for initial and continuing review and approval.

quote: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(a) requires the composition of the drug product, including identity and quantity of each ingredient.
error: 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(a) is the drug substance. The drug product (components, composition, manufacture, controls) is 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(b). The same wrong cite is used for the drug product on lines 90, 100, 115, 126, 588 and 596.
correct: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(7)(iv)(b) for the drug product. (a)(7)(iv)(a) is the drug substance.

quote: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(5) requires a summary of previous human experience, including prior clinical trials, foreign marketing experience, and any adverse events.
error: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(5) is the investigator's brochure. Previous human experience is 312.23(a)(9). The same wrong cite appears on lines 611, 619, 642 and 517.
correct: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(9) (Previous human experience with the investigational drug).

quote: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(3)(iv) and Form 1571 require identification of the phase of clinical study.
error: 312.23(a)(3)(iv) is the overall investigational plan for the following year. Identifying the phase(s) is required on the cover sheet at 312.23(a)(1)(ii). The same wrong cite is on lines 657 and 665.

quote: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(3)(ii) requires a description of the objectives and planned duration of the proposed clinical investigation.
error: 312.23(a)(3)(ii) is the brief summary of previous human experience. The broad objectives and planned duration are in the introductory statement at 312.23(a)(3)(i). The reference on line 687 repeats it.

quote: Form FDA 1571 Item 4 requires the name of the investigational drug.
error: On Form FDA 1571, Item 4 is the sponsor telephone number and Item 5 is the name of the drug. Other item numbers are also off: Item 3 (line 733) is the sponsor address, not the IND number (Item 6). Item 11 (line 665) is the submission content type, not the phase (Item 8). Item 10 (line 333) is the serial number, not the manufacturing site.
correct: 1571: Item 5 drug name, Item 6 IND number, Item 8 phase. No 1571 item identifies the manufacturing site.

quote: Pharmacokinetic data including absorption, bioavailability, half-life, volume of distribution, and clearance are expected per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(13)(ii)
error: Pharmacokinetics is not at 21 CFR 201.57(c)(13)(ii). That paragraph covers in vitro/animal activity data. Pharmacokinetics (12.3) is under (c)(13)(i). The same wrong citation is at line 455.
correct: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(13)(i), Clinical Pharmacology, which includes 12.3 Pharmacokinetics.

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(6), the Use in Specific Populations section must address dosing in hepatic and renal impairment
error: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(6) is Warnings and Precautions. Use in Specific Populations is (c)(9). The same wrong citation is at line 478.
correct: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(9), Use in Specific Populations (8.x).

quote: The instructions must be tested for comprehension.
error: Neither 21 CFR 201.57(c)(18) nor FDA's 2022 IFU guidance requires comprehension testing of an IFU. It is presented here as a requirement.
correct: Label comprehension or human factors testing is recommended in some cases (for example, combination products under the human factors guidance), but 201.57/IFU rules do not require it.

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(16), the labeling must describe all available dosage forms, strengths, NDC numbers, and packaging configurations
error: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(16) is References (section 15). How Supplied/Storage and Handling is (c)(17). The same wrong citation is at lines 572, 573 and 596.
correct: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(17), How Supplied/Storage and Handling (section 16).

quote: Per 21 CFR 201.57(c)(14), the Drug Abuse and Dependence section must include the controlled substance schedule
error: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(14) is Nonclinical Toxicology (section 13). Drug Abuse and Dependence is (c)(10). The same wrong citation is at line 766.
correct: 21 CFR 201.57(c)(10), Drug Abuse and Dependence (section 9).

quote: Medical and Education Policy) reviewer performing labeling review
error: DMEPA is the Division of Medication Error Prevention and Analysis, not the 'Division of Medical and Education Policy'. The expansion starts on line 831.
correct: DMEPA = Division of Medication Error Prevention and Analysis (CDER Office of Surveillance and Epidemiology).

quote: A cover letter is required under 21 CFR 314.50(a) as part of the application form
error: 21 CFR 314.50(a) requires the application form (Form FDA 356h). It does not require a cover letter. A cover letter is recommended by guidance only.
correct: 314.50(a) requires Form FDA 356h. A cover letter is recommended by FDA guidance and goes in Module 1.2.

quote: Include a cover letter in Module 1.0
error: In the US regional Module 1, cover letters go in section 1.2, not 1.0.
correct: Module 1.2 (Cover letters).

quote: The ISE is required under 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) to integrate efficacy results across studies
error: 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(vi)(b) is the safety update report requirement (the 4-month safety update), not the ISE. The integrated summary of effectiveness is at 314.50(d)(5)(v). The wrong cite is repeated in the reference on line 138.
correct: The ISE is required under 21 CFR 314.50(d)(5)(v).

quote: A 505(b)(2) application must identify the listed drug(s) relied upon and include a right-of-reference letter or suitability petition per 21 CFR 314.54.
error: What defines a 505(b)(2) application is that it relies on investigations the applicant has no right of reference to. A suitability petition (21 CFR 314.93) belongs to the ANDA pathway. Neither document is required under 314.54. The question on line 293 makes the same claim.
correct: A 505(b)(2) application must identify the listed drug(s) or published literature relied upon, with patent certifications and exclusivity statements (314.54, 314.50(i)). No right-of-reference letter or suitability petition is required.

quote: Patent certifications (Paragraph I-IV) are required under 21 CFR 314.50(i) for any drug product with listed patents in the Orange Book.
error: Paragraph I-IV certifications under 314.50(i) apply to 505(b)(2) applications, for patents on the listed drug relied upon. A 505(b)(1) NDA submits patent information on its own patents under 314.53 and makes no paragraph certifications. The rule fires for any NDA, including 505(b)(1).
correct: Paragraph I-IV certifications (314.50(i)) are required for 505(b)(2) applications against patents on the listed drug relied upon. 505(b)(1) applicants submit patent information under 314.53.

quote: include the payment confirmation or fee waiver/reduction request in Module 1.2 of the eCTD submission
error: In the US regional Module 1, section 1.2 is cover letters. The user fee cover sheet (Form FDA 3397) goes under 1.1 Forms.
correct: Module 1.1 (Forms), 1.1.2 user fee cover sheet, Form FDA 3397.

error: 314.126(b)(2)(v) describes historical controls, which have nothing to do with pre-specifying the analysis. The analysis requirement is at 314.126(b)(7), and the protocol/objectives requirement is at (b)(1).
correct: 21 CFR 314.126(b)(7) (adequate analysis of results), with (b)(1) for the protocol.

quote: a pre-specified multiplicity adjustment is required per ICH E9 Section 5.7
error: ICH E9 Section 5.7 covers subgroups, interactions and covariates. Multiplicity is in Section 5.6 (Adjustment of Significance and Confidence Levels). The same wrong section appears in the reference on line 478.
correct: ICH E9 Section 5.6 covers multiplicity adjustment.

quote: the standard NDA review clock is 10 months (Standard Review) or 6 months (Priority Review) from the filing date
error: Under PDUFA VII, review goals run from the 60-day filing date only for NME NDAs and original BLAs under 'the Program'. For non-NME NDAs, the 10-month and 6-month goals run from the receipt date.
correct: NME NDAs and original BLAs: 10 or 6 months from the 60-day filing date (12 or 8 months from receipt). Non-NME NDAs: 10 or 6 months from receipt.

quote: to allow pre-approval inspections under 21 CFR 314.110
error: 21 CFR 314.110 covers complete response letters. It is not the authority for pre-approval inspections.
correct: Pre-approval inspection rests on FD&C Act 704 and the refusal-to-approve grounds in 21 CFR 314.125(b) (e.g. (b)(1), (b)(12)), carried out under Compliance Program 7346.832.

quote: expects applicants to have sufficient manufacturing capacity per FD&C Act Title X
error: The drug shortage provisions are Title X of FDASIA (2012), codified at FD&C Act section 506C and following. The FD&C Act itself has no 'Title X' on drug shortages. The reference on line 620 repeats the error.
correct: FDASIA Title X; FD&C Act section 506C; 21 CFR 314.81(b)(3)(iii).

quote: Under PREA (FD&C Act Section 505B), all NDAs must contain a pediatric assessment or an approved pediatric study deferral or waiver. A PSP must be submitted and agreed upon before the NDA is filed.
error: PREA applies only to applications for a new active ingredient, new indication, new dosage form, new dosing regimen or new route of administration, and orphan-designated indications are exempt. It does not apply to all NDAs. The question on line 758 repeats 'all NDAs'.
correct: PREA applies to NDAs for a new active ingredient, indication, dosage form, dosing regimen or route, and orphan indications are exempt. Those applications must include a pediatric assessment, or a waiver or deferral, and an agreed iPSP must be submitted (within 60 days of the End-of-Phase 2 meeting, per 505B(e)).

quote: FDA Guidance: In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies (2020); FDA Guidance: Clinical Drug Interaction Studies (2020)
error: These two January 2020 FDA guidances were replaced when FDA adopted ICH M12 'Drug Interaction Studies' as final guidance (August 2024). They are cited here as current.
correct: ICH M12 Drug Interaction Studies (FDA final guidance, 2024).

quote: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(iv) requires non-clinical laboratory studies including bench performance testing to support device safety and effectiveness.
error: 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(iv) is the summary's 'marketing history' item. Nonclinical laboratory studies are required by 814.20(b)(6)(i). The same wrong cite appears at lines 98, 120-121 (biocompatibility), 632-633 (shelf life) and 865 (IEC 60601).
correct: Cite 21 CFR 814.20(b)(6)(i), the technical section on nonclinical laboratory studies (microbiological, toxicological, immunological, biocompatibility, stress, wear, shelf life and other lab or animal tests).

quote: A complete device description is required per 21 CFR 814.20(b)(3)(i), including pictorial representations, engineering drawings, and descriptions of all functional components.
error: 814.20(b)(3)(i) is the summary's indications-for-use item. The summary device description is (b)(3)(ii), and the complete description of the device, its components and principles of operation is (b)(4)(i).
correct: Cite 21 CFR 814.20(b)(4)(i), with (b)(3)(ii) for the summary description.

quote: Design outputs must satisfy design inputs per 21 CFR 820.30(d), and the relationship must be traceable through a design history file.
error: 21 CFR 820.30 (design controls) was removed when the QMSR took effect 2026-02-02 and is cited here as in force. The file does this throughout: 820.30(d)/(i) at line 194, 820.75 at 586-587, 820.50 at 609-610, 820.30(j) at 657-658, 820.30(e)/(f) at 683-684, 820.30(i) at 706-707, 820.30 at 737, and 820.30(g) at 761-762. Under the old QSR, 820.30(i) was design changes, not traceability, so lines 194 and 706 were wrong even before.
correct: Cite 21 CFR Part 820 (QMSR) via ISO 13485:2016 clauses 7.3.x (design and development), 7.5.6 (process validation, including sterilization), 7.4 (purchasing) and 7.3.10 (design and development files). Mark the old 820.30/820.50/820.75 cites as former QSR.

quote: PMA submissions must identify the advisory panel per 21 CFR 814.20(b)(1).
error: 814.20(b)(1) asks only for the applicant's name and address. No paragraph of 814.20 requires the applicant to identify an advisory panel. Line 327 makes the same claim.
correct: 814.20(b)(1) is the applicant name and address. Panel and classification come from 21 CFR Parts 860-892 and the product code. PMA content does not require a panel identification.

quote: Devices must be manufactured under a quality system per 21 CFR 820 (Quality System Regulation). ISO 13485 certification is expected for PMA-class devices.
error: The QSR was replaced by the QMSR on 2026-02-02. Part 820 now incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference. FDA does not require or expect ISO 13485 certification. Line 561 ('document compliance with 21 CFR 820 QSR') has the same problem.
correct: 21 CFR Part 820 (QMSR, effective 2026-02-02) incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference. Compliance is required; third-party certification is not an FDA requirement.

quote: 21 CFR 820.30(i); ISO 13485:2016 Section 7.3.9; FDA Design Control Guidance (1997)
error: ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3.9 is 'Control of design and development changes', not traceability. 21 CFR 820.30(i) was also design changes, and it is removed under the QMSR.
correct: Traceability runs through 7.3.3-7.3.7 (inputs, outputs, verification, validation) and 7.3.10 (design and development files) of ISO 13485:2016.

quote: recommended to inform the risk analysis per ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.2
error: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.2 is 'Management responsibilities'. It does not deal with adverse event data from similar devices (also cited at line 837).
correct: Clause 5.4 (identification of hazards, which uses information on similar devices) and Clause 10 (production and post-production activities, collection of information) are the relevant clauses.

quote: A descriptive study title is required per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(a) and is fundamental for IND submission identification.
error: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(a) requires a statement of objectives and purpose. It does not require a study title.
correct: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(a) requires a statement of the study's objectives and purpose. A protocol title is expected by ICH E6(R3) Appendix B, not by this paragraph.

quote: ICH E9 Section 2.3.2 requires that blinding be appropriate to minimize bias when using placebo controls.
error: ICH E9 Section 2.3.2 is Randomisation. Blinding is Section 2.3.1.
correct: ICH E9 Section 2.3.1 (Blinding).

quote: Randomization is applicable only to multi-arm studies per ICH E9 Section 2.3.1.
error: ICH E9 Section 2.3.1 is Blinding. Randomisation, including stratification, is Section 2.3.2. Lines 246, 440 and 441 repeat the miscitation.
correct: ICH E9 Section 2.3.2 (Randomisation).

quote: The study phase must be declared per 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(a) to allow FDA to assess developmental appropriateness.
error: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(6)(iii)(a) requires a statement of the study's objectives and purpose. Identifying the phase is required on the cover sheet (Form FDA 1571), 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(iv).
correct: 21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)(iv) requires identification of the phase or phases of the clinical investigation.

quote: ICH E9 Section 2.2.1; 21 CFR 314.126(b)(2)(v)
error: 21 CFR 314.126(b)(2)(v) is the historical control type, not endpoint definition. ICH E9 Section 2.2.1 is 'Population'; primary and secondary variables are Section 2.2.2. Line 346 also attributes primary-endpoint definition to E9 Section 2.2.1.
correct: ICH E9 Section 2.2.2 (Primary and Secondary Variables). 21 CFR 314.126(b)(6) requires well-defined and reliable methods of assessing response.

quote: Pre-specification of statistical methods is required per ICH E9 Section 5.1 and 21 CFR 314.126(b)(2)(v).
error: 21 CFR 314.126(b)(2)(v) describes historical controls, not pre-specification of the statistical analysis. Line 417 repeats it.
correct: 21 CFR 314.126(b)(7) requires an analysis of results adequate to assess the drug's effects. ICH E9 Section 5.1 covers pre-specification.

quote: ICH E9 Section 3.5; FDA Guidance: Missing Data in Confirmatory Clinical Trials (2020)
error: FDA has issued no guidance titled 'Missing Data in Confirmatory Clinical Trials (2020)'. That title belongs to the EMA guideline (EMA/CPMP/EWP/1776/99 Rev. 1, 2010).
correct: EMA Guideline on Missing Data in Confirmatory Clinical Trials (2010), or ICH E9(R1) (estimands and sensitivity analysis), or the National Research Council report 'The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials' (2010) commissioned by FDA.

quote: ICH E9 Section 2.3.4 addresses the need for adequate washout to avoid carryover effects.
error: ICH E9 has no Section 2.3.4 (Section 2.3 has only 2.3.1 Blinding and 2.3.2 Randomisation). Washout and carryover are discussed under crossover designs in Section 3.1.2. Line 646 repeats it.
correct: ICH E9 Section 3.1.2 (Cross-over Design) discusses carryover and washout periods.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 7.1; ISO 14971:2019 Clause 9 (traceability)
error: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 9 is the risk management review (the risk management report), not traceability.
correct: Traceability for each hazardous situation is required by ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5 (risk management file).

quote: MDR 2017/745 Annex I; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4; MDCG 2021-24
error: MDCG 2021-24 is the guidance on classifying medical devices under MDR Annex VIII. It does not cover GSPR mapping or technical documentation.
correct: Drop MDCG 2021-24. GSPR mapping and the technical documentation fall under MDR Annex I and Annex II (Section 4, the GSPR checklist).

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 8 requires that when individual residual risks are judged acceptable but the overall residual risk has not been evaluated, a benefit-risk analysis shall be performed.
error: This misstates Clause 8. Clause 8 requires an evaluation of the overall residual risk against the plan's criteria. A benefit-risk determination comes in only if the overall residual risk is not judged acceptable. Benefit-risk is not mandatory just because the overall risk has not been evaluated.
correct: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 8 requires the manufacturer to evaluate the overall residual risk against the method and criteria in the risk management plan. If that risk is not judged acceptable, the manufacturer may gather and review data to decide whether the medical benefits outweigh it; otherwise the overall residual risk remains unacceptable.

quote: ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.2 emphasizes data-driven estimation.
error: ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.2 is 'Initiating a Quality Risk Management Process'. Risk assessment, including risk analysis and estimation, is Section 4.3. The same misnumbering appears on lines 117 and 258.
correct: ICH Q9(R1) Section 4.3 (Risk Assessment) covers risk identification, analysis and evaluation.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4; MDCG 2021-24
error: Cites MDCG 2021-24 (device classification guidance) as support for traceability in the risk management file.
correct: Drop MDCG 2021-24. ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5 and MDR Annex II already support this point.

quote: ISO 14971:2019 Clause 4.5; MDR 2017/745 Annex II Section 4; FDA 21 CFR 820.30(g)
error: 21 CFR 820.30(g) (QSR design validation) was removed when the QMSR took effect on 2026-02-02. It is cited here as if still in force.
correct: Cite 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR, which incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference, including clause 7.1 risk management and 7.3 design and development), or mark 820.30(g) as the former QSR provision.

quote: ICH E3 Section 12.3.1 requires that individual patient narratives include patient demographics to contextualize the adverse event.
error: ICH E3 Section 12.3.1 is the listing of deaths, other SAEs and other significant AEs. The patient narratives are in Section 12.3.2. Lines 69, 92, 114, 115 and 235/236 cite 12.3.1 for narrative content in the same way.
correct: ICH E3 Section 12.3.2 (Narratives of deaths, other serious adverse events, and certain other significant adverse events).

quote: ICH E3 Section 12.3.1; ICH E2B(R3) Section 2.2; CIOMS VI Section 3.1
error: ICH E2B(R3) does not number its data elements as 'Section 2.x'. The elements are C (report identification), D (patient: D.7 medical history, D.9 death/autopsy), E (reaction/event), G (drug) and H (narrative). The citations to E2B(R3) Sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 2.6, 2.12.x and 2.14 (lines 69, 91, 114, 141, 212, 312, 337, 362, 384) point to provisions that do not exist.
correct: Cite the E2B(R3) data element: D.1-D.6 for patient characteristics, D.7 for medical history, G.k for drug information (concomitant drugs included), D.9 for death details and autopsy, E.i for reaction/event and seriousness, G.k.9 for drug-reaction assessment and dechallenge/rechallenge.

quote: SUSAR was reported ${daysSinceEvent} days after the event, exceeding the ${isFatal ? '7-day (fatal/life-threatening)' : '15-day'} regulatory reporting deadline.
error: The regulatory clock does not start at the event date. Under 21 CFR 312.32(c) and ICH E2A it starts when the sponsor first receives the information and determines it qualifies (day 0). Counting from the event misstates whether a deadline was missed.
correct: The 7/15 calendar-day clock runs from the sponsor's initial receipt of the information (21 CFR 312.32(c)(1) and (c)(2); ICH E2A III.B), not from the date of the event.

quote: ICH E2A Section IV.A requires expedited reporting of SUSARs: 7 calendar days for fatal/life-threatening events, 15 calendar days for all other serious events. 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1) mandates IND safety reports within these timeframes.
error: ICH E2A has no Section IV. Reporting time frames are in Section III.B. Also, 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1) sets only the 15-day IND safety report. The 7-day report for unexpected fatal or life-threatening suspected adverse reactions is 312.32(c)(2). The timelines apply to serious unexpected suspected adverse reactions, not to all serious events. The same nonexistent 'Section IV.A' appears on lines 266, 486 and 487.
correct: ICH E2A Section III.B: 7 calendar days for fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs (complete report within 8 more days) and 15 calendar days for other serious unexpected ADRs. 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1) is the 15-day report; 312.32(c)(2) is the 7-day report. Both run from the sponsor's initial receipt of the information.

quote: ICH E2A Section III.B requires an assessment of the causal relationship between the drug and the event.
error: ICH E2A Section III.B is reporting time frames, not causality assessment. The same miscitation recurs on lines 362, 384/385 ('III.B.a'), 407/408 and 430/431.
correct: Causality comes in through the ADR definition in ICH E2A Section II.A.2 (a reasonable possibility of a causal relationship); the factors for assessing it are in Attachment 2.

quote: ICH E2A Section IV.A requires unblinding for SUSAR determination.
error: ICH E2A has no Section IV. Managing blinded therapy cases is Section III.D.
correct: ICH E2A Section III.D (Managing blinded therapy cases) recommends breaking the blind for the individual patient when a serious unexpected ADR is a candidate for expedited reporting.

quote: ICH E2A Section IV.B requires notification to all regulatory authorities where the IND/CTA is active.
error: ICH E2A has no Section IV.B. Line 191 also cites a nonexistent 'ICH E2A Section IV'.
correct: Expedited reporting standards are in ICH E2A Section III. Informing investigators and IRBs/ECs is Section III.H. US IND safety reports go to FDA and all participating investigators under 21 CFR 312.32(c)(1).

quote: ICH E2E Section IV requires ongoing signal detection and evaluation throughout clinical development.
error: ICH E2E (Pharmacovigilance Planning) is numbered 1-4 plus an Annex; there is no Section IV or V (cited here and on lines 680, 704, 731). E2E covers planning for the early post-marketing period, not signal detection during clinical development.
correct: ICH E2E Section 2 (Safety Specification) and Section 3 (Pharmacovigilance Plan) apply to post-authorisation pharmacovigilance planning. Signal management in development comes under the DSUR (ICH E2F).

quote: Per 21 CFR 211.186, every batch production and control record must be identifiable.
error: 21 CFR 211.186 covers master production and control records. Batch production and control records are 21 CFR 211.188. The same text appears again at line 74.
correct: 21 CFR 211.188 covers batch production and control records; 211.186 covers master production and control records.

quote: Under 21 CFR 820.40, how does your document control system track this procedure without a unique identifier?
error: 21 CFR 820.40 (former QSR document controls) was removed when the QMSR took effect on 2026-02-02, but it is cited as in force. The same removed section is cited as current at lines 107, 112, 114, 164, 174, 179, 181, 213, 214, 466, 475, 480, 482, 499, 508, 513, 516, 533, 542, 547, 549, 580, 582, 734, 743, 748, 750, 783, 818, 971 and 973.
correct: Device document control now falls under ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.4, incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR, effective 2026-02-02). If 820.40 is cited at all, it should be marked 'former QSR'.

quote: 21 CFR 211.22(d) requires written procedures for production and process controls.
error: 211.22(d) says the responsibilities and procedures of the quality control unit must be in writing and followed. Written procedures for production and process control are 211.100(a).
correct: 21 CFR 211.22(d): the QCU's responsibilities and procedures must be in writing and followed. Production and process control procedures: 21 CFR 211.100(a).

quote: 21 CFR 820.20(a) requires a quality policy that includes compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.
error: 21 CFR 820.20 (management responsibility) was removed by the QMSR, effective 2026-02-02, but is cited as current here and at lines 147, 248, 893 and 894 (820.20(b)(1)).
correct: Management responsibility and quality policy are now ISO 13485:2016 clause 5, incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR).

quote: 21 CFR 820.75 requires documented procedures for process validation.
error: 21 CFR 820.75 was removed by the QMSR (effective 2026-02-02) but is cited as in force here and in the reference at line 282.
correct: Process validation is now ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.5.6, incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR).

quote: 21 CFR 820.90(a) requires procedures for controlling nonconforming product.
error: 21 CFR 820.90 was removed by the QMSR (effective 2026-02-02) but is cited as current here and at line 315.
correct: Control of nonconforming product is now ISO 13485:2016 clause 8.3, incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR).

quote: Per 21 CFR 820.90, you are required to establish procedures for corrective and preventive action.
error: Even under the former QSR, 820.90 was Nonconforming product and CAPA was 820.100. Both sections were also removed when the QMSR took effect on 2026-02-02. The same mis-citation repeats at lines 341, 346 and 348 (reference).
correct: CAPA is now required by ISO 13485:2016 clauses 8.5.2 and 8.5.3, incorporated by reference through 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR). The former QSR CAPA section was 820.100.

quote: 21 CFR 820.25 requires that training effectiveness be assessed.
error: The former QSR 820.25(b) required training to be documented, with defect-awareness requirements. It did not require verification of training effectiveness; that comes from ISO 13485 6.2. 820.25 was also removed by the QMSR. Lines 407 and 412 repeat the claim ('shall include verification of training effectiveness'). 820.25 is cited as current again at lines 380, 381, 414, 449, 1089 and 1090.
correct: Training-effectiveness evaluation is required by ISO 13485:2016 clause 6.2(d), incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR). The former 820.25 is no longer in force.

quote: 21 CFR 820.40 requires periodic review.
error: The former 820.40 had no periodic-review requirement, and it has been removed in any case (QMSR, 2026-02-02). Line 613 repeats the claim ('implicitly requires periodic review') and line 608 repeats the question.
correct: No FDA device or drug cGMP regulation mandates a fixed SOP periodic-review interval. Review frequency is a firm-defined practice; ISO 13485 4.2.4 requires review and update of documents as necessary.

quote: 21 CFR 820.184 requires that device records be retained for the design and expected life of the device, but no less than two years from product release.
error: The retention requirement was in the former 820.180(b), not 820.184 (Device history record). Both sections were removed by the QMSR (effective 2026-02-02). Line 685 repeats the citation.
correct: Under the QMSR, record retention follows ISO 13485:2016 clause 4.2.5 (at least the device's lifetime, and no less than 2 years from release) via 21 CFR 820.10, together with 21 CFR 820.35. The former retention section was 820.180(b).

quote: 21 CFR 820.30(g) requires risk analysis for device design.
error: 21 CFR 820.30 (design controls) was removed by the QMSR (effective 2026-02-02) but is cited as in force here and at line 717.
correct: Design controls are now ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.3, with risk management per clause 7.1 / ISO 14971, incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10.

quote: 21 CFR 820.70(a) requires that process parameters be documented.
error: 21 CFR 820.70 was removed by the QMSR (effective 2026-02-02) but is cited as current here and at line 931.
correct: Production and process controls are now ISO 13485:2016 clause 7.5, incorporated by 21 CFR 820.10 (QMSR).

quote: 21 CFR 211 (cGMP), 21 CFR 820 (QSR), ICH E6(R3) (GCP), and 21 CFR Part 11 (electronic records).
error: This client-facing auditor description calls 21 CFR 820 the QSR. Part 820 has been the Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR) since 2026-02-02.
correct: 21 CFR 820 (QMSR, incorporating ISO 13485:2016 by reference).

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.2 mandates stability data on at least three batches
error: Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.2 is Stress Testing. The three-batch requirement is in Selection of Batches. The same wrong section is cited at lines 70 and 237.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.3 (drug substance) and Section 2.2.3 (drug product), Selection of Batches.

error: 21 CFR 211.166(a)(3) is about reliable, meaningful and specific test methods, not storage conditions.
correct: 21 CFR 211.166(a)(2), storage conditions for samples retained for testing.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.2 requires accelerated studies at 40 ± 2 °C / 75 ± 5% RH
error: Q1A(R2) 2.2.7.2 covers drug products packaged in impermeable containers. The long-term, intermediate and accelerated conditions, and the significant-change rule, are all in 2.2.7.1 (General case). The same wrong section is cited at lines 116, 675 and 676.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.7.1 (General case).

quote: ICH Q1B; ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.6
error: Q1A(R2) 2.2.6 is Testing Frequency. Drug product photostability is 2.2.2.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.2, Photostability Testing.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.2 requires that stability studies be conducted on the drug product packaged in the container closure system proposed for marketing.
error: Q1A(R2) 2.2.2 is Photostability Testing. Container closure is 2.2.4. Also, 21 CFR 211.166(a)(2), cited at line 162, covers storage conditions for samples, not testing in the marketed container.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.4, Container Closure System; 21 CFR 211.166(a)(4), which requires testing in the same container-closure system the drug is marketed in.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.8 recommends testing at intervals sufficient to establish the stability profile
error: Q1A(R2) 2.2.8 is Stability Commitment. Testing frequency is 2.2.6. The same wrong citation is at line 214.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.6, Testing Frequency.

quote: ICH Q1E Section 4 limits shelf-life extrapolation
error: ICH Q1E has no Section 3 or 4. Its body is Section 1 (Introduction) and Section 2 (Guidelines), plus Appendices A and B. 'Section 4', 'Section 4.1', 'Sections 3-4' and 'Sections 2-4' are also cited at lines 116, 313, 434, 676, 701 and 702.
correct: ICH Q1E Section 2.3 (Extrapolation), 2.4 (Data evaluation, including 2.4.1 and 2.4.2) and Appendix A/B. Extrapolation is up to 2x and no more than 12 months beyond the long-term data, when supported by statistics and there is no significant change at accelerated conditions.

quote: require stability testing at 30 ± 2 °C / 65 ± 5% RH (Zone III) or 30 ± 2 °C / 75 ± 5% RH (Zone IVa/IVb) for tropical markets.
error: The climatic zones are assigned the wrong conditions. Zone III (hot/dry) is not 30°C/65% RH, and Zone IVa is not 30°C/75% RH.
correct: WHO TRS 953 Annex 2 long-term conditions: Zone III 30°C/35% RH; Zone IVa 30°C/65% RH; Zone IVb 30°C/75% RH.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.6 requires stress testing to elucidate intrinsic degradation pathways
error: Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.6 is Testing Frequency, not stress testing. The same wrong section is cited at lines 411, 456 and 457.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.2, Stress Testing.

quote: 21 CFR 211.68; 21 CFR 211.166; FDA Guidance: Equipment Qualification (2004)
error: There is no FDA guidance titled 'Equipment Qualification (2004)'.
correct: Cite 21 CFR 211.63/211.68 and the FDA Process Validation Guidance (2011) for equipment/utility qualification, or ISPE/ASTM E2500 as industry practice.

quote: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.2.9 states that in-use stability studies should be conducted for multi-dose products
error: Q1A(R2) 2.2.9 is Evaluation, and Q1A(R2) does not set an in-use stability requirement.
correct: In-use stability is covered by the EMA Note for Guidance on In-Use Stability Testing of Human Medicinal Products (CPMP/QWP/2934/99), not by Q1A(R2) 2.2.9.

quote: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1) requires the applicant to provide a stability commitment including the number of batches per year to be placed on long-term stability and the protocol to be followed.
error: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1) is the NDA Field Alert Report requirement. It has nothing to do with stability commitments. The same wrong citation appears at lines 589, 590, 599, 601, 724 and 725.
correct: Stability protocols and commitments go in the application under 21 CFR 314.50(d)(1)(ii)(a) (with 211.166). Ongoing stability results are reported in the annual report under 314.81(b)(2) (CMC, (b)(2)(iv)). 314.81(b)(1) is the field alert report, due within 3 working days.

quote: FDA Guidance on OOS Results (2006) provides a framework for laboratory investigation of unexpected test results.
error: The 2006 OOS guidance was superseded by Revision 1 (May 2022). The 2006 date is repeated at line 647.
correct: FDA Guidance: Investigating Out-of-Specification (OOS) Test Results for Pharmaceutical Production, Revision 1 (May 2022).

quote: 21 CFR 314.81(b)(1); ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.7
error: Q1A(R2) 2.1.7 is drug substance Storage Conditions, not the stability commitment. 314.81(b)(1) is the field alert report.
correct: ICH Q1A(R2) Section 2.1.8 / 2.2.8, Stability Commitment.
